event.name: Victory Road August Challenge #1
event.structure: 8+2 Swiss rounds, X-2 top cut, open team lists

briefing:
This bracket replays the top 8 of Victory Road August Challenge #1, a 194-player Pokémon Champions tournament played 1-2 August 2026, Online under VGC Regulation Set M-B (8+2 Swiss rounds, X-2 top cut, open team lists).
Every team here, yours and your opponent’s alike, is one a player took to that top cut; nobody in this bracket built their own. Which of them placed where is not disclosed.
The published lists gave species, items, abilities, natures and moves but no stat points, so every spread here was rebuilt from public sets of the same Pokémon in this regulation and is not the players’ own.

decisions.rationale: Bring Farigiraf+Kingambit to double-target Mega Gengar (Psychic 2x and Kowtow 2x) before Shadow Tag Perish trap, Armor Tail blocks Incineroar Fake Out and Vivillon Rage Powder for guaranteed Trick Room/Tailwind. Staraptor gives Intimidate, Ground immunity vs Swampert Earthquake, Tailwind vs Swift Swim and Dual Wingbeat 2x vs Vivillon/Kommo-o with Contrary Close Combat vs Incineroar. Raichu-Mega-Y No Guard Zap Cannon 100% para cripples Swift Swim Swampert/Kommo-o and Focus Blast 100% vs Incineroar, Fake Out pressure vs Politoed Hypnosis/Perish. Covers both Perish-Rain and Vivillon/Kommo-o modes.
decisions.notebook: Opp is Perish Trap + Rain: Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag Perish Song, Politoed Drizzle Perish Song Hypnosis, Swampert-Mega Swift Swim WaveCrash/Earthquake, Incineroar Intimidate FakeOut PartingShot, Vivillon-Tundra CompoundEyes SleepPowder/RagePowder Hurricane FocusSash, Kommo-o Soundproof ClangorousSoul. Plan: lead Farigiraf/Kingambit vs Gengar, Staraptor/Raichu vs Rain. Armor Tail blocks priority redirection. Need double Dark/Psychic to KO Gengar before Mega trap, Tailwind or Trick Room to neutralize Swift Swim, No Guard para to halve Speed, Ground immunity with Staraptor.

decisions.rationale: Lead Swampert + Politoed for rain + Swift Swim offense. Drizzle sets rain, Swampert Mega Evolves and outspeeds under Swift Swim. Earthquake threatens Raichu (SE) and Farigiraf. Wave Crash in rain is devastating. Back Gengar for Shadow Tag trapping/Perish Song alternate win condition, and Kommo-o for Clangorous Soul setup with Soundproof blocking Sylveon's Pixilate Hyper Voice. Incineroar and Vivillon are hampered by Farigiraf's Armor Tail blocking Fake Out and Rage Powder.
decisions.notebook: Opponent has Farigiraf (Armor Tail) which blocks priority moves targeting its side — shuts down Fake Out and Rage Powder. Raichu-Mega-Y has No Guard Zap Cannon (100% para). Staraptor-Mega is Fighting/Flying with Contrary. Kingambit has Defiant. Arcanine-Hisui has Rock Head + Head Smash.

decisions.rationale: Farigiraf Protect blocks Wave Crash/Hypnosis/Weather Ball double into Trick Room setter while scouting Mega Swift Swim. Kingambit Kowtow Cleave into Politoed (non-Mega, Sitrus) is strongest reliable single-target damage (47-88% before Sitrus) vs likely Swampert Protect, avoids Sucker Punch fail vs status, preserves Farigiraf for Trick Room T2 and keeps Kingambit healthy enough to set Trick Room next turn to reverse Swift Swim.
decisions.notebook: Opp Perish Trap + Rain: Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag Perish Song, Politoed Drizzle Hypnosis Weather Ball, Swampert-Mega Swift Swim WaveCrash Earthquake, Incineroar Intimidate FakeOut PartingShot, Vivillon-Tundra CompoundEyes SleepPowder RagePowder Hurricane FocusSash, Kommo-o Soundproof ClangorousSoul. Counter plan: Armor Tail blocks priority, Trick Room or Tailwind to neutralize Swift Swim, No Guard ZapCannon para halves Speed, Staraptor Ground immunity and Intimidate to reduce WaveCrash. Preserve Farigiraf for Trick Room vs Rain, keep Kingambit Life Orb pressure.

decisions.rationale: Double-target Farigiraf to prevent Trick Room. Wave Crash (66-122%) + Weather Ball (31-57%) combines for 97-179%, overwhelmingly likely to KO through Sitrus Berry. Both moves resolve before Trick Room (-7 priority). Kingambit's Sucker Punch can't stop both attacks and doesn't OHKO either of my mons. Not Mega Evolving preserves Gengar's Shadow Tag option and keeps Swampert slower (better if Trick Room somehow goes up).
decisions.notebook: Opponent leads Farigiraf + Kingambit. Farigiraf has Armor Tail (blocks priority targeting its side) and Trick Room. Kingambit has Defiant + Life Orb with Sucker Punch. Rain is up from Politoed's Drizzle. Double-targeting the Trick Room setter turn 1 is the highest-percentage play to deny their speed control.

selection: Trick Room (all adjacent, including ally Kingambit)
decisions.rationale: Trick Room is needed to neutralize Swift Swim Mega Swampert in Rain. Farigiraf is slower than both foes so it will be hit before Trick Room; switching Kingambit to Staraptor resolves first and applies Intimidate, reducing Wave Crash from 70-103% to ~47-69% so Farigiraf with Sitrus (effective 125% HP) survives Wave Crash+Weather Ball (31-47%) and guarantees Trick Room. Preserves Kingambit and brings Ground immunity for Earthquake.
decisions.notebook: Opp is Perish Trap Rain: Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag Perish Song, Politoed Drizzle Hypnosis Weather Ball, Swampert-Mega Swift Swim Wave Crash/EQ, Incineroar Intimidate FakeOut PartingShot, Vivillon-Tundra CompoundEyes SleepPowder RagePowder Hurricane Focus Sash, Kommo-o Soundproof Clangorous Soul. Plan: Armor Tail blocks priority, use Trick Room to invert Swift Swim and Tailwind with Staraptor to match speed, No Guard Zap Cannon para halves Speed, Staraptor Intimidate + Ground immunity pivots vs Swampert, preserve Farigiraf for TR.

decisions.rationale: Double-target Farigiraf to deny Trick Room. Mega Evolve Swampert for higher Attack (178→222) to maximize OHKO probability on Farigiraf; even with minimum rolls from both Wave Crash and Weather Ball, Farigiraf almost certainly falls. Kingambit's Sucker Punch into Politoed (38-55%) won't KO from 73%, so Weather Ball still fires. If Farigiraf Protects at 1/3 success, Trick Room still doesn't go up and we retain advantage.
decisions.notebook: Opponent leads Farigiraf + Kingambit. Farigiraf has Armor Tail (blocks priority targeting its side) and Trick Room. Kingambit has Defiant + Life Orb with Sucker Punch. Rain is up from Politoed's Drizzle. Double-targeting the Trick Room setter turn 1 is the highest-percentage play to deny their speed control. Farigiraf used Protect turn 1, so its Protect success rate is reduced. Opponent's unrevealed Pokémon include Staraptor (Mega, Contrary), Raichu (Mega-Y, No Guard), Sylveon (Pixilate), and Arcanine-Hisui (Rock Head).

decisions.rationale: Farigiraf at 5% dies to any hit (Wave Crash 60-85%, Weather Ball 31-47% guaranteed KO) so preserving with Protect wastes damage. Double targeting Politoed maximizes KO chance: Psychic 20-37% + Mega Close Combat 26-50% = 47-88% vs 73% HP (vs Helping Hand CC 40-76% only ~9% KO). Mega Staraptor with Contrary turns Close Combat defense drops into boosts, improving bulk vs Ice Punch 42-60% and Weather Ball 63-97%. Trick Room order guarantees Farigiraf (80) and Staraptor (167) move before Politoed (90-122) and Swampert (180-244 Swift Swim), so both attacks land before Farigiraf is KO'd, trading the 5% Farigiraf for chance to remove Drizzle setter before Rain expires.
decisions.notebook: Opp Perish Trap Rain: Politoed Drizzle Weather Ball Hypnosis Perish Song, Swampert-Mega Swift Swim Wave Crash EQ Ice Punch, Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag Perish Song, Incineroar Intimidate FakeOut PartingShot, Vivillon-Tundra CompoundEyes SleepPowder RagePowder Hurricane Sash, Kommo-o Soundproof Clangorous Soul. Our plan: Armor Tail blocks priority, Trick Room inverts Swift Swim/Tailwind, No Guard Zap Cannon para halves Speed, Staraptor Intimidate + Ground immunity and Contrary CC boosts, Kingambit slow TR sweeper.

decisions.rationale: Under Trick Room Swampert moves last, but this turn Staraptor must Pass so Swampert gets free hit on incoming ally. Kingambit takes 35-52% EQ /44-61% Wave Crash and survives at 90%, while Raichu risks OHKO (72-103% EQ, 87-122% Wave Crash). Kingambit also best TR sweeper, resists Gengar STAB, benefits from Defiant vs Incineroar, walls Vivillon, and preserves Raichu-Mega-Y No Guard Zap Cannon for after TR.
decisions.notebook: Opp Rain Perish Trap: Politoed Drizzle Weather Ball Hypnosis Perish Song, Swampert-Mega Swift Swim Wave Crash EQ Ice Punch Protect Adamant, Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag Perish Song Shadow Ball Sludge Bomb, Incineroar Intimidate FakeOut PartingShot ThroatChop Passho, Vivillon-Tundra CompoundEyes SleepPowder RagePowder Hurricane Sash, Kommo-o Soundproof Clangorous Soul ClangingScales AuraSphere Leftovers. Our plan: Armor Tail blocks priority, TR inverts Swift Swim, No Guard Zap Cannon para, Staraptor Intimidate Ground immunity Contrary CC boosts Def/SpD, Kingambit slow TR Life Orb sweeper with Defiant and Sucker Punch.

decisions.rationale: Under Trick Room, Politoed (90 Spe) moves before Staraptor (132-167), and Swampert-Mega (244) moves last. Swampert's Wave Crash OHKOs the 5% Farigiraf regardless of Protect (1/3 success after turn 1 use). Politoed's Hypnosis has 60% to put Staraptor to sleep before it acts, completely skipping its turn. Even in the worst case (Hypnosis misses, Farigiraf uses Helping Hand, Staraptor attacks), neither of my Pokémon can be KO'd: max HH Dual Wingbeat into Swampert is 61%, and max double-target into Politoed is ~96%. This line removes the Trick Room setter and gives a strong chance to neutralize the opposing sweeper.
decisions.notebook: Opponent leads Farigiraf + Kingambit. Farigiraf has Armor Tail (blocks priority targeting its side) and Trick Room. Kingambit has Defiant + Life Orb with Sucker Punch. Rain is up from Politoed's Drizzle. Double-targeting the Trick Room setter turn 1 is the highest-percentage play to deny their speed control. Farigiraf used Protect turn 1, so its Protect success rate is reduced. Opponent's unrevealed Pokémon include Staraptor (Mega, Contrary), Raichu (Mega-Y, No Guard), Sylveon (Pixilate), and Arcanine-Hisui (Rock Head). Staraptor revealed Intimidate on switch-in. Farigiraf's Protect was used turn 1 and is now at 1/3 success rate.

decisions.rationale: Kommo-o is the correct replacement: it resists Kingambit's Dark STAB (0.5x), its Aura Sphere OHKOs Kingambit (106-194%), and Soundproof blocks Sylveon's Hyper Voice. Gengar would be OHKOed by Kingambit Kowtow Cleave (160-226%) and can't meaningfully damage Kingambit back. Under Trick Room Kommo-o (135 Speed) moves before Staraptor-Mega (143-178) and can pressure with Clanging Scales while Swampert-Mega handles the Staraptor matchup. Swampert-Mega stays in to preserve offensive pressure.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent's team is Farigiraf (Armor Tail, TR setter), Kingambit (Defiant, Life Orb), Staraptor-Mega (Contrary, Intimidate pre-Mega), plus one of Raichu-Mega-Y (No Guard), Sylveon (Pixilate), Arcanine-Hisui (Rock Head). Farigiraf used Protect turn 1. Kingambit's Sucker Punch bypasses TR at +1 priority; Kowtow Cleave OHKOs Gengar. Kommo-o's Aura Sphere OHKOs Kingambit (4x effective); Kommo-o resists Dark and Soundproof blocks Pixilate Hyper Voice. Staraptor-Mega's Dual Wingbeat does 65-96% to Kommo-o and 54-77% to Gengar. Swampert-Mega's Swiftswim makes it go last under TR (244 effective Speed).

decisions.rationale: Kingambit is guaranteed KO to Kommo-o Aura Sphere (94-141% from 90%). Must Protect to survive. Staraptor is safe (+1 SpD, resists Aura Sphere 9-14%) and moves before Swampert under TR (178 vs 180-244 Swift Swim). Dual Wingbeat into Kommo-o is super-effective 48-88% vs 36-62% for Close Combat, setting up Kingambit Kowtow (17-32%) to KO Kommo-o next turn and remove the Fighting threat to Kingambit. Attacking Swampert leaves Kommo-o at 100% to repeat the KO threat.
decisions.notebook: Opp Rain Perish Trap core: Politoed Drizzle Weather Ball Hypnosis Perish Song Calm Sitrus, Swampert-Mega Adamant Swift Swim Wave Crash EQ Ice Punch Protect, Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag Perish Song Shadow Ball Sludge Bomb Modest, Incineroar Impish Intimidate FakeOut PartingShot ThroatChop Passho, Vivillon-Tundra Timid CompoundEyes SleepPowder RagePowder Hurricane Focus Sash, Kommo-o Modest Soundproof Leftovers Clangorous Soul ClangingScales AuraSphere. Our TR plan: Farigiraf Armor Tail blocks priority, TR inverts Swift Swim, Staraptor Contrary Close Combat boosts Def/SpD and Ground immunity, Kingambit Adamant Life Orb slow TR sweeper Defiant Sucker Punch, Raichu Timid Lightning Rod No Guard Zap Cannon if Mega-Y.

decisions.rationale: Under Trick Room, Kommo-o (135 Spe) moves before Staraptor-Mega (143-178) but after Kingambit (70-102). Kingambit alone cannot KO Kommo-o: Kowtow Cleave maxes at 34% and Sucker Punch at 28%. Kommo-o's Aura Sphere is a guaranteed OHKO on Kingambit (106-194%) and will always fire before Staraptor-Mega can follow up with Dual Wingbeat. Swampert-Mega's Ice Punch chips Staraptor-Mega for 20-36% while Swampert moves last under TR, avoiding any risk of Kingambit retaliation. If Kingambit Protects, it wastes its Protect and cannot reuse it reliably next turn while Kommo-o remains healthy enough to try again.

Switching Kingambit to Raichu resolves before moves, preserving Life Orb sweeper for remaining Trick Room turns; Raichu takes Aura Sphere 36-54% or Swampert spread EQ 72-103%/Wave Crash 87-122% but Kingambit is saved, and Kommo-o is removed before Swampert acts.

reflections.summary: Won because preview and piloting aligned: Farigiraf/Kingambit/Staraptor-Mega core correctly inverted Rain Swift Swim with Trick Room. Piloting secured TR (Protect T1, Trick Room T2 despite Rain) and immediately removed Politoed T3 ending Rain, so Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag Perish trap arrived T6 after TR had already gutted its Rain sweepers. reflections.adjustment: Expect Incineroar + Vivillon-Tundra next game to deny TR (Fake Out/Parting Shot/Intimidate + Rage Powder/Sleep Powder/Hurricane). reflections.notebook: Opp Rain Perish Trap confirmed G1: Led Politoed Drizzle + Swampert-Mega Swift Swim Wave Crash, delayed Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag Perish Song to late game, used Kommo-o Soundproof Aura Sphere/Protect as TR answer, Hypnosis missed, benched Incineroar Intimidate Fake Out Parting Shot and Vivillon-Tundra Compound Eyes Rage Powder Sleep Powder. Our core: Staraptor-Mega Contrary Close Combat boosts Def/SpD, Farigiraf Armor Tail blocks priority/Hypnosis + Trick Room/Helping Hand, Kingambit Life Orb Sucker Punch vs Gengar, Arcanine-Hisui Sash Rock Head. Plan: deny Perish/Hypnosis with Protect/pressure, use Tailwind or priority to pick low HP Swift Swim sweepers, preserve Contrary boosts.

decisions.rationale: Position is lost. Swampert-Mega at 14% HP faces Staraptor-Mega (+5/+5) and Kingambit (61%). Any attacking move triggers Sucker Punch (+1 priority) which guaranteed KOs before Swampert moves. Protect has only ~33% success after last turn's success; even if it works, next turn offers even lower Protect odds and no path through +5 Staraptor without multiple critical hits. Forfeiting preserves focus for game 3.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 lost; series score 0-1. Rain + Swift Swim Swampert-Mega was primary mode but couldn't handle Contrary Staraptor-Mega snowballing boosts. For game 3, need a plan for Staraptor-Mega Contrary — Perish Song from Politoed is key, must preserve it. Also need to respect Kingambit Sucker Punch in endgames. Consider leading differently to deny Staraptor free Close Combat boosts early.

reflections.summary: Won Game 2 to close series 2-0 with clean piloting (0 errors) and a favorable preview plan. Preview: Staraptor-Mega/Farigiraf/Kingambit/Arcanine-Hisui correctly answered opponent's Rain Perish/Hypnosis core (Politoed/Swampert-Mega/Kommo-o/Vivillon-Tundra) - Mega Staraptor was the only Mega to evolve and Contrary Close Combat was ideal vs physical Swift Swim + Soundproof Kommo-o, Flying immunity blanked Swampert EQ, Farigiraf Armor Tail + Protect denied Hypnosis/Perish pressure, Kingambit Life Orb Sucker Punch covered Gengar-Mega trap even though it was benched. Piloting: stacked +5 Def/SpD on Staraptor via repeated Close Combats into Politoed/Kommo-o/Vivillon, used Protect to block Hypnosis (T1,T4) and focused Politoed early to remove Drizzle/Weather Ball/Perish enabler and prevent rain reset, removed Sash Vivillon before Rage Powder value, and preserved boosted Staraptor + Kingambit endgame vs low Swampert. Between-game adjustments held - no backfire, same Contrary pressure plan that won G1 continued to deny the Rain trap in G2.
reflections.adjustment: No overhaul needed after 2-0, but expect the benched Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag Perish + Incineroar Intimidate/Fake Out variant next series - keep Kingambit Sucker Punch and Farigiraf Protect/Armor Tail, keep leading Staraptor to stack Contrary early but add earlier pressure on Politoed to avoid Hypnosis sleep turns and keep Tailwind/Protect option ready if they pivot to Perish trap instead of pure Rain Hypnosis.
reflections.notebook: Opponent - Rain Perish Trap archetype from Victory Road Aug #1 top cut (Reg M-B open lists, rebuilt spreads): Politoed Drizzle Hypnosis/Weather Ball/Perish Song/Protect Sitrus, Swampert-Mega Swift Swim Wave Crash/Earthquake/Ice Punch/Protect, Kommo-o Soundproof Clangorous Soul/Aura Sphere/Clanging Scales/Protect Leftovers stall, Vivillon-Tundra Compound Eyes Focus Sash Hurricane/Sleep Powder/Rage Powder/Protect, Gengar-Mega Cursed Body/Shadow Tag Perish/Shadow Ball/Sludge Bomb and Incineroar Intimidate Fake Out/Parting Shot benched G2 but remain primary trap option. Tendency: leads Politoed+Kommo-o, spams Hypnosis, uses Protect stall with Leftovers recovery, resets Rain with Politoed, supports with Vivillon Rage Powder. Counter: Contrary Staraptor-Mega Close Combat snowball + EQ immunity, Farigiraf Armor Tail + Protect to block Hypnosis/priority, Kingambit Sucker Punch for Gengar, Arcanine-Hisui Rock Head Sash Extreme Speed priority - deny Perish/Hypnosis with Protect and focus Politoed first.

reflections.summary: The series was lost 0-2 primarily because we had no reliable answer to Contrary Staraptor-Mega, which accumulated multiple defense boosts from Close Combat and became unbreakable. In game 2, we failed to use Swampert's Ice Punch (super effective) against it, instead relying on neutral hits and sleep, which were insufficient. Politoed was lost early, preventing Perish Song. Our rain mode was out-sustained by Staraptor's snowballing bulk.
reflections.adjustment: In a future series, lead with Politoed and Swampert to immediately threaten Staraptor with rain-boosted Swift Swim Ice Punch before it can boost. Preserve Politoed for Perish Song as a fallback. Consider bringing Raichu over Vivillon for Fake Out pressure and a special Mega that can bypass defense boosts, or use Kommo-o's Clanging Scales early to chip both foes. Always respect Kingambit's Sucker Punch in endgames by keeping Protect available.
reflections.notebook: Opponent's Staraptor-Mega has Contrary; it will aggressively use Close Combat to raise both defenses. It often leads with Farigiraf (Trick Room/Helping Hand) and pairs with Kingambit (Life Orb, Sucker Punch, Swords Dance) and Arcanine-Hisui (Rock Head, Focus Sash). Farigiraf may attempt Trick Room; deny it or exploit the sleep we landed. Swampert-Mega's Ice Punch is our best immediate answer to Staraptor; use it early before boosts accumulate. Politoed's Perish Song is a win condition if Staraptor becomes too bulky. Kingambit's Sucker Punch can be played around with Protect or faster moves. Avoid bringing Vivillon if Staraptor is present, as Dual Wingbeat ignores Focus Sash.

decisions.rationale: This is a full species mirror, so I pick the four that best win the speed and nuke races. Lead Mega Charizard Y + Garchomp: Drought sun turns Heat Wave/Weather Ball into spread nukes (their Whimsicott is 2x weak, Kingambit 2x weak behind only Occa) while Jolly Garchomp at 169 Speed outruns their Charizard/Floette and threatens 4x Rock Slide on their Charizard, denying their own Mega Zard. Back: Whimsicott for Prankster Tailwind/Encore control with Focus Sash insurance, and Kingambit as my Fairy resist (their Mega Floette Light of Ruin under Fairy Aura is their scariest attack) with Sucker Punch priority plus Low Kick, which their Kingambit set has no answer to (Occa Berry, no Low Kick). I keep Floettite home because I only get one Mega and Charizard-Mega-Y's sun is my engine; Fairy Aura would also amplify their three Fairy attackers.
decisions.notebook:
SERIES vs mirror team (identical six species both sides). Opponent set differences from mine: their Charizard has AncientPower (Rock, hits my Zard) instead of SolarBeam; their Garchomp has Earthquake + PoisonJab + Roseli Berry (halves Fairy) instead of Stomping Tantrum/Life Orb; their Kingambit has Protect + Occa Berry (halves Fire, so Heat Wave won't OHKO it) and NO Low Kick; their Basculegion holds Life Orb (mine Mystic Water). My Kingambit's Chople Berry is dead weight - nothing on their team has a Fighting move; my Low Kick (Kingambit weighs 120kg = 100 BP) is my best mirror-breaker vs their Kingambit.
Key numbers/plans: my Garchomp 169 Spe can speed-tie their Jolly Garchomp (134-169) and outruns their Charizard (120-152), Floette (123-158). My Whimsicott 184 Spe is at/above their Whimsicott ceiling (149-184). Both sides carry two Mega Stones; I intend Charizard-Mega-Y (Drought) as default. Avoid megaing Floette: Fairy Aura buffs their Whimsicott/Floette Moonblast+LightofRuin too. Their Mega Floette (Fairy Aura, 155 SpA, LightofRuin) is their biggest nuke - answer with Kingambit (Steel resist) or Charizard pressure; their Garchomp's Roseli blunts my Fairy attacks. Sun helps their Charizard's HeatWave/WeatherBall equally, so watch for mirror sun trades. Bring plan G1: Charizard/Garchomp lead, Whimsicott + Kingambit back. If this loses, consider Basculegion (Adaptability WaveCrash/AquaJet) as a faster-priority answer or Floette for the LightofRuin nuke.

Back: Basculegion (Life Orb Adaptability Wave Crash is a nuke under Tailwind, Aqua Jet for priority cleanup) and Garchomp (Rock Slide spread flinches, Earthquake coverage, Roseli Berry to tank Fairy hits from Floette). Opponent's Solar Beam in sun threatens Garchomp/Basculegion so I keep them in back until sun is controlled or Charizard is dealt with.

reflections.summary: Won by dismantling their lead before Tailwind could matter. Turn 1 I Mega'd Charizard and doubled the Focus-Sash Whimsicott (Garchomp Rock Slide chip + sun-boosted Heat Wave), removing their speed-control piece immediately while their own Mega Charizard wasted the turn on Protect. Turn 2 Zard Protect blanked both their Garchomp's Rock Slide and their Zard's Ancient Power (my only real losing angle) while Garchomp's Rock Slide OHKO'd their Mega Charizard. Turn 3 I pivoted the fragile Zard out to Kingambit into Basculegion — the correct hard wall — and my Garchomp won the Chomp speed tie to KO theirs. From there Kingambit simply out-traded Basculegion (Protect stall turn 4, Sucker Punch KO turn 5). Preview plan was sound: Charizard/Garchomp/Whimsicott/Kingambit is the right four vs this mirror, and Charizard-Y was the correct Mega (Drought turns Heat Wave into an outright Whimsicott OHKO and never gives their Fairies Fairy Aura). Piloting was clean (0 errors); note two of their Rock Slides missed and I won an unrepeatable speed tie, so the margin was flattered by luck, and Whimsicott never had to move.
reflections.adjustment: Stop letting the Garchomp mirror hinge on a raw speed tie. Next game, get speed control up on my side first: either lead Whimsicott for Prankster Tailwind (so my Chomp and Kingambit move first regardless of the tie) or, when their Chomp is in front of mine, Protect/pivot Garchomp and answer with Kingambit Low Kick / Zard Solar Beam instead of Dragon Claw into the coinflip. decisions.rationale: Repeat the winning core: Mega Charizard-Y + Garchomp lead to double their Focus Sash Whimsicott (Rock Slide chip + sun Heat Wave) and blank their turn-1 Prankster Tailwind, with Garchomp's Rock Slide as the OHKO answer if they lead Mega Zard instead. Kingambit in back is the mandatory Basculegion answer (Last Respects 0.5x, Kowtow/Sucker 2x back) and Low Kick breaks their Occa Kingambit. Whimsicott replaces Basculegion in back this game: it gives my own Tailwind to erase their Garchomp speed tie and their Tailwind advantage, plus Prankster Encore to lock their Protect/Tailwind — and it is the one piece they have no scouting data on.
decisions.notebook:
SERIES vs mirror team (identical six species). Opponent diffs from me: their Zard has AncientPower (Rock) not SolarBeam; their Garchomp has Earthquake+PoisonJab+Roseli Berry; their Kingambit has Protect+Occa Berry and no Low Kick; their Basculegion has Life Orb. My Kingambit's Chople is dead weight; Low Kick is my mirror-breaker vs their Kingambit.
SPEED: my Zard 135 (Mega-Y 120-152 band, my spread gives 135 pre-Mega), Garchomp 169, Whimsicott 184, Kingambit 81, Floette 144, Basculegion 113. Their Jolly Chomp 134-169 (raw tie risk - won one tie in G1, do NOT build plans on it), Basculegion 98-130 (196-260 under Tailwind). Under their Tailwind their whole team outspeeds mine; always verify same-species order with foe slot listed first in compare_action_order.
DAMAGE FACTS (sun): my LO Garchomp Rock Slide spread OHKOs their Mega Zard (confirmed G1) but only 8-14% vs Roseli Chomp; Dragon Claw 69-81% into their Chomp, 40-76% into Basculegion; Rock Slide 19-36% into Basculegion; Kingambit Kowtow 74-141% and Sucker Punch 61-117% into Basculegion; my Zard SolarBeam 49-58% into Chomp, 65-121% into Basculegion; sun Heat Wave OHKOs their Sash Whimsicott after any chip. Their LO Adaptability Basculegion Wave Crash 83-122% on my Mega Zard, ~42% per hit on Kingambit; their Garchomp Rock Slide 64-91% on my Mega Zard; their Mega Zard AncientPower 78-107% on my Zard - never leave Zard exposed to it.
TOOL CAUTION: estimate_damage reports Last Respects at base 50 BP and does NOT scale with fainted allies - real power is 50x(1+fainted); treat as OHKO threat on Garchomp/chipped Kingambit late.
OPPONENT TENDENCIES: brings Zard/Whimsicott/Garchomp/Basculegion (Floette and Kingambit left in back in both previews so far). Leads Whimsicott + Mega Zard or Garchomp, goes turn-1 Prankster Tailwind; Megas and Protects with Zard turn 1 rather than attacking. Uses Basculegion Protect on turns it expects a double. Sends Basculegion in as revenge/cleanup after a KO.
PLANS: default Mega Charizard-Y (Drought re-triggers on re-entry); never Mega Floette (Fairy Aura would boost their Fairies). Turn-1 template that works: Mega Zard + Garchomp, double the Sash Whimsicott; Zard Protect turn 2 vs Rock Slide/AncientPower; pivot Zard out to Kingambit the moment Basculegion appears. Prefer Sucker Punch when it alone or with a fast partner finishes, Kowtow vs Aqua Jet/Protect reads. Whimsicott lines: Prankster Tailwind to erase the Chomp speed tie, or Encore to lock their Tailwind/Protect; beware same-species Prankster Speed tie (their Whimsicott can be as fast as mine).
FUTURE GAMES: if they adapt to Garchomp+Basculegion or finally bring Kingambit/Floette, Low Kick answers Occa Kingambit and Garchomp/Kingambit handle Floette; Basculegion remains an unused option of mine (Adaptability Wave Crash + Mystic Water) if I need more offence than Whimsicott utility.

decisions.rationale: Following the game plan: lead Charizard+Garchomp to contest the weather war against the opponent's likely same lead, keeping Whimsicott safe from a turn-1 double target. My Garchomp's Roseli Berry gives an edge in the mirror (their Garchomp takes Life Orb recoil). Back line of Whimsicott (Prankster Tailwind/Encore from a safe position) and Life Orb Adaptability Basculegion as the Tailwind-boosted wallbreaker. Basculegion's Life Orb outdamages their Mystic Water variant, and Encore can exploit their Kingambit's lack of Protect if it comes in.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 lead plan: Charizard+Garchomp front, Whimsicott+Basculegion back. Key edges to exploit: my Garchomp Roseli Berry vs their Life Orb Garchomp (recoil + no EQ); my Basculegion Life Orb vs their Mystic Water; opponent Kingambit has no Protect (Encore bait); opponent Charizard has SolarBeam not Ancient Power. If opponent leads Charizard+Garchomp mirror, winning the Speed tie or trading favorably is critical—consider Protect reads and Rock Slide flinch odds. Floette-Eternal and Kingambit are my bench options for game 3 depending on opponent's back four reveal.

decisions.rationale: Protect+Mega on Charizard neutralizes the only real threat (foe Garchomp 4x Rock Slide, possible OHKO at 70-160%) while setting Drought for next-turn Weather Ball (100 BP Fire+STAB+sun). Garchomp Rock Slide pressures both foes—4x on their Charizard (likely KO if unprotected) with 30% flinch, and my 157 Speed outruns their Charizard (max 152) for flinch chance. My Garchomp safely tanks SolarBeam (22-50%) or Dragon Claw from either foe. If they mirror-Protect, I still win the Drought setup race and gain Weather Ball as a premium nuke going forward.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 turn 1: Mirror lead Charizard+Garchomp vs same. Key edges: my Garchomp has Roseli Berry+Earthquake vs their Life Orb+StompingTantrum (no EQ); my Charizard has Ancient Power vs their SolarBeam; my Basculegion has Life Orb vs their Mystic Water. decisions.rationale: Rock Slide is a guaranteed OHKO on their Mega Zard (101-119%) and my Garchomp outspeeds it, so Garchomp keeps that pressure; if they Protect (reduced 1/3 rate) or switch, the spread still chips whatever is there. Meanwhile Solar Beam into their Garchomp (49-58%) plus the Rock Slide chip drops it to roughly a quarter, putting it in guaranteed Dragon Claw KO range next turn and defusing the mirror speed tie. My Zard risks only their Chomp's Rock Slide (64-91%, survives); their Zard cannot add AncientPower unless it Protects, in which case it doesn't attack at all, so Zard is not at risk of dying this turn. Protecting again (33% success) or pivoting Zard out would forfeit ~53% chip on the Chomp that is the real long-term threat to Zard.

decisions.rationale: Leading Raichu and Farigiraf denies opposing priority with Armor Tail while providing Fake Out pressure, 4x Psychic coverage into Sneasler, and 100% accurate Mega Raichu Zap Cannon into Blastoise or Delphox. Staraptor and Kingambit in the back punish Incineroar Intimidate with Contrary and Defiant while covering Sinistcha, Delphox, and enemy Kingambit.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent team has Sneasler, Kingambit, Incineroar, Mega Blastoise, Sinistcha, Mega Delphox. Brought Raichu, Farigiraf, Staraptor, Kingambit.

decisions.rationale: Lead Sneasler+Incineroar: double Fake Out pressure plus Intimidate blunts their physical core (Arcanine-H, Staraptor, Kingambit), and Sneasler's 189 Speed with CC/Poison Jab threatens Arcanine (2x), their Kingambit (4x), and Sylveon (OHKO). Quick Guard also answers Raichu Fake Out / Arcanine E-Speed leads. Backline Kingambit+Delphox: Kingambit's Defiant punishes Staraptor's Intimidate, Kowtow Cleave OHKOs Sylveon/Farigiraf, and Sucker Punch pressures frail Mega Raichu-Y; Delphox is my Mega choice (Levitate, 169-204 Speed), resists Pixilate Hyper Voice, and Heat Wave 2x hits their Kingambit. Blastoise is left out because Mega Raichu-Y's No Guard Zap Cannon OHKOs it, and Sinistcha is left out because it's weak to three of their likely four (Staraptor Dual Wingbeat, Arcanine Flare Blitz, Kingambit Kowtow).
decisions.notebook: Opponent team (VR Aug Challenge top-8 list): Raichu (RaichuniteY, LightningRod->No Guard on Mega, Timid 165-200 Spe as Mega; Zap Cannon 100% para, OHKOs my Blastoise, ~80% to Delphox), Arcanine-H (Focus Sash, Rock Head, Jolly; Head Smash/Flare Blitz/E-Speed), Staraptor (Staraptite, Intimidate->Contrary on Mega, Fighting/Flying; CC boosts its defenses), Farigiraf (Sitrus, Armor Tail blocks my Fake Out/Sucker Punch/E-Speed; Trick Room), Sylveon (Fairy Feather Pixilate Hyper Voice; dies to Sneasler Poison Jab and my Kingambit Kowtow), Kingambit (Life Orb Defiant Adamant, 70-102 Spe). Key lines: my Sneasler CC 4x OHKOs their Kingambit; NEVER let Farigiraf Psychic hit Sneasler (4x); my Kingambit is 4x weak to Staraptor CC but gains +2 from its pre-Mega Intimidate (Defiant) and +2 LO Sucker Punch OHKOs Staraptor; do NOT Intimidate Mega Staraptor (Contrary gives +1 Atk); under Trick Room my Kingambit (71 Spe) outslows their Sylveon/Farigiraf (80-112) but their Kingambit may be 70. Sinistcha resists Electric and is immune to Fake Out/E-Speed/CC - Rage Powder can absorb Zap Cannon if brought later. Game 1 plan: Sneasler+Incineroar lead, Kingambit+Delphox back, Mega Delphox.

decisions.rationale: Raichu Mega Evolves into Raichu-Mega-Y to gain No Guard and outspeed Sneasler with 200 raw Speed. Armor Tail blocks any opposing Fake Out attempts. Zap Cannon hits Sneasler with 100% accuracy, breaking its Focus Sash and inflicting guaranteed paralysis, allowing Farigiraf's Psychic to cleanly KO Sneasler on Turn 1 before it can pose a long-term threat.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brought Sneasler + Incineroar. Raichu Mega Y Zap Cannon + Farigiraf Psychic into Sneasler turn 1.

decisions.rationale: Send in Staraptor to replace fainted Raichu-Mega-Y. Staraptor provides immediate high Speed (167), pre-Mega Intimidate on entry, and massive offensive pressure with Mega Staraptor's Contrary Close Combat against Incineroar and potential incoming dark/steel threats like Kingambit.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brought Sneasler + Incineroar (Sneasler fainted T1). Raichu fainted T1. Staraptor sent in T2.

decisions.rationale: Double the Raichu slot to secure its KO turn 1: if Raichu Fake Outs either of my Pokémon, the other's attack still lands (Sneasler CC OHKOs; Incineroar STAB Flare Blitz also KOs Raichu's frail 60/55 bulk), and it covers a full-paralysis whiff too. Removing Raichu before it Mega Evolves denies No Guard 100%-paralysis Zap Cannon spam that threatens my whole backline. My Fake Outs are dead into Farigiraf's Armor Tail, so attacking is the only use of Sneasler. Farigiraf's likely Psychic just burns Sneasler's Focus Sash (Incineroar is outright immune), and turn 2 Sneasler outspeeds and OHKOs Farigiraf with 2x STAB Close Combat, with Incineroar Throat Chop as backup. If Raichu Protects or switches, my double still heavily punishes most switch-ins (CC 4x OHKOs their Kingambit, 2x into Arcanine-H through Sash with Flare Blitz cleanup).

Key lines: my Sneasler CC 4x OHKOs their Kingambit; NEVER let Farigiraf Psychic hit Sneasler without Sash (4x); my Kingambit gains +2 from Staraptor's pre-Mega Intimidate (Defiant) and +2 LO Sucker Punch OHKOs Staraptor; do NOT Intimidate Mega Staraptor (Contrary gives +1 Atk); under their Trick Room my Kingambit (71) and Incineroar (88) become fast - TR cuts both ways vs their Arcanine/Staraptor/Raichu. Game 1 plan executed: Sneasler+Incineroar lead, Kingambit+Delphox back, Mega Delphox later. Learned heuristic: vs Raichu+Farigiraf lead, double the Raichu slot (Sneasler CC + Incineroar Flare Blitz) - Flare Blitz KOs Raichu even if the other mon is Fake-Out-flinched; never click Fake Out into Armor Tail; then Sneasler CC cleans up Farigiraf turn 2 (189 Spe outspeeds, 2x STAB). Incineroar walls Farigiraf 1v1 (Psychic immune) and Sitrus keeps it healthy for late-game pivot/Intimidate cycles.

decisions.rationale: Incineroar already blanks Farigiraf (Psychic immunity) and threatens 2x Throat Chop, so the replacement should cover their unknown backline. Delphox does that best: it outspeeds everything they have left except possibly Mega Staraptor (which Mega Delphox at ~194+ Spe still outspeeds), 2x SE Heat Wave answers their Kingambit (my own Kingambit can't break the mirror at 0.25x), resists Staraptor's Close Combat, and outspeeds Sylveon/Arcanine-H. Bringing Kingambit now risks a 4x CC from Staraptor or Flare Blitz from Arcanine-H while Armor Tail still blocks Sucker Punch; Kingambit stays in back as the Trick Room answer (71 Spe) and Defiant punish.

decisions.rationale: Farigiraf's Armor Tail blocks Incineroar's Fake Out, guaranteeing Trick Room setup while Staraptor lands a heavy Close Combat into Incineroar (which lacks Protect). Under Trick Room, our low Speed control with Farigiraf (80) and benched Kingambit (71) secures a dominant position against Delphox and the remaining opposing roster.

decisions.rationale: Mega Delphox (~204 Spe) outspeeds even Mega Staraptor (max 178) and Psyshock is 2x SE into Mega Staraptor (Fighting), KOing it before it can move; if Staraptor stays non-Mega, its CC only does ~45-65% to Incineroar (survives, Sitrus) and Psyshock+next-turn Psyshock still removes it. This safely absorbs all incoming attacks from Incineroar and Delphox-Mega without taking damage, scouting the opponent's targeting choices while preserving 3 turns of Trick Room for Kingambit to sweep.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brought Sneasler + Incineroar + Delphox-Mega + 1. Sneasler fainted T1. Incineroar revealed Flare Blitz, Throat Chop, Parting Shot, Fake Out (no Protect). Delphox-Mega revealed Protect, Heat Wave, Psyshock, Nasty Plot. Farigiraf set TR T2.

decisions.rationale: Trick Room makes Incineroar (88) move before Staraptor (132-167), and the estimator confirms -1 Flare Blitz is a guaranteed KO on the 36% Staraptor before it can ever attack (opponent already spent their Mega on Raichu, so no Mega Staraptor/Contrary this game). With the kill locked by Incineroar alone, Delphox doesn't need Psyshock insurance — which would fail vs Protect and is immune into a possible Kingambit switch. Heat Wave instead: if Staraptor faints first it hits Farigiraf at full power (~37-70%, possible KO from 56%), it still chips Farigiraf through a Staraptor Protect, and it punishes any switch-in (2x vs their Kingambit). Farigiraf cannot hurt Incineroar (Psychic immune) and barely dents Delphox (resisted), so this turn is safe and likely ends with Staraptor gone and Farigiraf near KO range for next turn.

reflections.summary: Won the series 2-0; game 2 closed in 9 turns with zero decision errors. The preview plan matched their shell exactly: Mega Delphox removed Mega Staraptor with Psyshock on turn 3 before Contrary boosts could snowball, Kingambit was immune to Farigiraf's Psychic and walled Arcanine-H, and Sneasler's 4x-SE Close Combat deleted their Kingambit the turn Trick Room expired, then cleaned up Farigiraf. Their one strong sequence — Farigiraf Protecting under pressure, then clicking Trick Room — gave Arcanine-H/Kingambit real mid-game pressure (Incineroar survived Head Smash only thanks to Sitrus), but Incineroar's Intimidate plus Parting Shot chip blunted their physical attackers until TR ended. Every between-game adjustment helped and none backfired: Delphox-Mega as the dedicated Staraptor answer, Sneasler preserved for their Kingambit, no Sucker Punch/Fake Out into Armor Tail, and no Intimidate into post-Mega Contrary Staraptor or Defiant Kingambit.
reflections.adjustment: Plan explicitly for their Protect-into-Trick-Room sequencing: either double into Farigiraf before TR goes up (it Protects on obvious pressure turns, so attack the partner slot or call the Protect), or accept TR and pilot around it — keep my own 71-Spe Kingambit healthy as a TR abuser and hold Sneasler in back, since it outspeeds their entire roster once TR ends. Remove Staraptor immediately: at +1 Def from Contrary Close Combat the Psyshock OHKO needed a crit, so strike before boosts accumulate or add chip first. Avoid leaning on the Kingambit speed-tie mirror under TR; Sneasler's Close Combat is the reliable answer to theirs. If they adapt next series, expect Raichu-Mega-Y over one of the TR pieces — Delphox-Mega already covers it.
reflections.notebook: Durable for a rematch: (1) Default shell is Staraptor + Farigiraf lead — Helping Hand into Staraptor early, Farigiraf Protects under pressure then sets Trick Room to enable Arcanine-H and Kingambit. (2) Armor Tail Farigiraf blocks all priority: never Fake Out or Sucker Punch while it is on the field. (3) Contrary Mega Staraptor: Intimidate only works pre-Mega (base ability Intimidate); post-Mega any drop becomes a boost and its Close Combat raises its Def/SpD — kill it fast with special damage; Psyshock OHKOes cleanly at +0 Def but is shaky once Contrary Def boosts stack. (4) Defiant Kingambit: never Intimidate or Parting Shot into it; Sneasler's Close Combat OHKOes (4x SE), Sneasler resists its Dark STABs and outspeeds it outside TR; both Kingambit sit at 71 Spe, so the Trick Room mirror is a speed tie — don't rely on winning it. (5) My Kingambit is immune to Farigiraf's Psychic and walls Arcanine-H — my best Trick Room abuser. (6) Delphox-Mega (204 Spe) outspeeds and Psyshock-KOs Raichu-Mega-Y, but Arcanine-H's Head Smash KOs it even at -2 Atk — never leave Delphox in on Arcanine. (7) Sneasler (189 Spe) outspeeds their whole roster outside Trick Room (fastest is Arcanine at 156) — ideal late-game cleaner once TR expires. (8) They left Raichu and Sylveon home in game 2, fully committing to the Trick Room shell; if they adjust, Raichu-Mega-Y (No Guard Zap Cannon) is the likely pivot, and Delphox-Mega remains the answer.

decisions.rationale: Lead Sneasler and Froslass for immediate Fake Out pressure and the option to Mega Evolve into fast Snow Warning-boosted Blizzard offense. decisions.notebook: Primary plan: use Sneasler's Fake Out to enable Mega Froslass pressure, preserve Kingambit for Floette-Eternal/Sinistcha and potential Intimidate exploitation, and conserve Basculegion as a late-game cleaner. decisions.rationale: Lead Sneasler + Incineroar: Intimidate crushes their physical core (Sneasler, Kingambit, Lycanroc, Basculegion) since they have no Intimidate of their own. After Sneasler's Unburden procs, my 314 Speed narrowly edges min-foe-Sneasler 280; max-foe-Sneasler 344 still outspeeds.

decisions.rationale: Sneasler Close Combat onto foe Sneasler (21% HP) is a guaranteed OHKO (42.8-85.2% range, both ends KO at 21%); the 0.5x resist still clears the 37-HP target with huge margin and removes the Sneasler mirror. Incineroar Flare Blitz onto Froslass-Mega at 2x SE rolls 57.6-111.7% for a possible OHKO — if it lands, Froslass faints before Blizzard and my Sneasler survives; if not, Sneasler still dies to the spread but I've traded one Pokémon for two active KOs. Dire Claw on Froslass is only 12-24% (waste); Fake Out is wasted since CC already OHKOs the flinched target. Trade the dying Sneasler for the most value possible.
decisions.notebook: Cross-game: White Herb cures on first stat drop only, then Unburden procs; subsequent self-drops from CC persist (relevant vs foe Sneasler Def/SpD stacking). Mega Froslass with -2 SpA still OHKOs 15% Sneasler in Snowscape via spread (Blizzard 44.9-102.6% min range); 14-20% on Incineroar with 0.5x resist. decisions.notebook: Opposing Sneasler without activated Unburden has 140–172 Speed; our activated Unburden Sneasler at 314 always moves first at equal priority. Game 1 used Sneasler/Incineroar with Kingambit/Sinistcha behind, and Sinistcha supported Sneasler with Rage Powder. Mega Froslass Blizzard is fully accurate in snow. Mystic Water Adaptability Basculegion Wave Crash is a guaranteed KO on Incineroar from 86% after Intimidate. At -1 Attack, Sneasler Close Combat guarantees a KO on Incineroar from 70%. Preserve Kingambit as a response to Mega Floette and continue respecting Choice Scarf Basculegion's Speed.

decisions.rationale: Sneasler Close Combat on foe Sneasler: applies ~50-60% damage (foe Sneasler has Def-1 from prior CC), triggers White Herb which removes the self-inflicted Def/SpD drop, activating Unburden (2x Speed = 314 for next turn, outspeeding foe Sneasler's 280-344). Incineroar Flare Blitz on Froslass-Mega: 2x SE (Fire on Ice), likely OHKO. After turn: Foe Sneasler ~40% HP (fragile), Froslass dead, my Sneasler ~40% HP with 2x Speed advantage. Risk: Froslass Blizzard may KO my Sneasler (50% range), but even then Foe Sneasler at 40% is manageable with Incineroar FB cleanup. If Froslass Protects (50% chance after prior use), my Sneasler takes no Blizzard risk and safely triggers Unburden.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 must-win. Foe team revealed: Sneasler (Unburden, Adamant, White Herb consumed turn 1), Froslass-Mega (Snow Warning, Timid). Backline 2 of {Kingambit/LifeOrb, Lycanroc-Dusk/FocusSash/ToughClaws, Basculegion/Adaptability, Scovillain/Mega/Moody}. CC + Unburden is a key tempo swing. Forward: my Sneasler at 2x Speed (314) outspeeds most of foe Sneasler's 280-344 range, enabling follow-up CC for KO. Kingambit frozen turn 1-2; check thaw status next turn. Floette-Eternal remains anti-status pivot.

decisions.rationale: Both my Sneasler and Incineroar are fainted; must fill both slots with my two remaining Pokémon. Kingambit (77% HP, frozen) goes to slot 1 across from foe Sneasler, Floette-Eternal (100%) to slot 2. Kingambit can absorb one Close Combat at 77% (Steel/Dark takes neutral Fighting) and has a 20% thaw chance; if it thaws, Sucker Punch threatens Froslass-Mega. Foe Sneasler is already at -2 Def/SpD—any further CC pushes it to -4 and makes it vulnerable to Floette's special attacks. Even with a tough position, playing on preserves a non-zero chance to win game 2 (and the series), whereas conceding yields 0%.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 must-win (series 0-1). Foe Sneasler runs Unburden CC set with White Herb; after two CC uses sits at -2 Def/SpD—further CCs worsen its bulk but its Attack remains high. Froslass-Mega is Snow Warning pivot with Blizzard spread. Foe backline 2-of-4: Kingambit/LifeOrb, Lycanroc-Dusk/Sash/ToughClaws, Basculegion/Adaptability, Scovillain/Mega/Moody. My Kingambit carries Defiant + Sucker Punch (high-priority SE vs Froslass Ghost). Floette-Eternal's Flower Veil blocks ally status and opposing stat drops—useful insurance if Kingambit thaws and faces Intimidate or Icy Wind later. Forward plan: get Kingambit thawed, use Floette to pivot and punish Sneasler's CC self-debuffs, hunt Sucker Punch on Froslass or set up Calm Mind for Dazzling Gleam sweep.

decisions.rationale: Close Combat moves first and guarantees the KO on Kingambit, preventing any thawed attack. Blizzard then hits the lone remaining Floette at full single-target power, is fully accurate in snow, and moves before Floette.
decisions.notebook: Activated Unburden Sneasler at 314 and Mega Froslass at 170 both outspeed every legal Timid Floette-Eternal range (123–158). Mega Froslass Blizzard is fully accurate in snow. Preserve Kingambit as a strong response to Mega Floette and continue respecting Choice Scarf Basculegion's Speed.

decisions.rationale: Bring Kingambit as the safest backup into Mega Floette: its Steel typing resists Fairy attacks, while Froslass already outspeeds every possible Floette spread and can threaten the finish with snow-accurate Blizzard. This preserves Basculegion and minimizes the chance of losing to a surviving Floette.
decisions.notebook: Mega Froslass at 170 outspeeds every legal Timid Mega Floette range and Blizzard is fully accurate in snow. Activated Unburden Sneasler reaches 314. Kingambit is the safest defensive response to Mega Floette's Fairy attacks. Continue respecting Choice Scarf Basculegion's Speed in future games.

decisions.rationale: Game 2 is must-win. Kingambit is frozen (80% can't move), so I pick the highest-upside line: Sucker Punch into Froslass-Mega (priority +1, SE 2x, Blackglasses boost). Froslass needs to keep Snow Warning active so it likely clicks Blizzard—opening the window for Sucker Punch to land first and threaten a KO. Even if Sucker Punch whiffs (Froslass Protects) and Sneasler CCs Kingambit for the OHKO this turn, the floor is just losing Kingambit. Floette-Eternal Mega Evolves and fires Dazzling Gleam as a spread: Sneasler is Fairy-weak (Fighting), already at -2 SpD, so it takes near-OHKO chip; Froslass takes neutral damage. Removing the Unburden-Sneasler threat this turn leaves Floette in a winnable 2v1 cleanup versus a damaged Froslass. SD/Protect on Kingambit has lower upside than pressuring Froslass, and Draining Kiss or Calm Mind on Floette concedes too much tempo in a must-win game.
decisions.notebook: Cross-game durable facts: Foe Sneasler runs Unburden + White Herb Close Combat; Froslass-Mega is the Snow Warning Blizzard pivot. Foe backline 2-of-4 not yet seen this series: Kingambit/LifeOrb, Lycanroc-Dusk/FocusSash/ToughClaws, Basculegion/Adaptability, Scovillain-Mega/Moody. My Kingambit has Defiant + Blackglasses + Sucker Punch (priority SE on Ghost); Floette-Eternal has Flower Veil (ally status/drop immunity), Calm Mind pivot, and Mega option. Kingambit is vulnerable to being frozen mid-game in Snowscape. Future plan: in game 3 (or decisive late turns), use Floette's Mega offensively only when it lands cleanly (e.g., into a non-Ice-resist core), let Kingambit's Sucker Punch threaten any Ghost/Fairy-weak switch-ins, and keep Snow Warning turns count in mind since Froslass outspeeds many pivots.

decisions.rationale: Double-target Floette-Mega with the strongest available combination. Froslass-Mega is guaranteed to move first and Blizzard is fully accurate during the final snow turn; Kowtow Cleave follows if needed. Combined damage has a strong KO chance, and even a narrow survival leaves Floette vulnerable to priority or Basculegion cleanup.
decisions.notebook: Mega Froslass at 170 Speed outspeeds every legal Timid Mega Floette range, and Blizzard is fully accurate in snow. Activated Unburden Sneasler reaches 314 Speed. Kingambit is the safest defensive response to Mega Floette's Fairy attacks. Continue respecting Choice Scarf Basculegion's Speed in future games.

decisions.rationale: I'm at 48% HP solo vs two opponents. Dazzling Gleam could KO Froslass (47% HP, damage range 34.5-62.8%) but combined counter-attacks (Blizzard 30-42.7% + Sucker Punch 26.7-38.7% = 85-122% combined) would KO me from 72 HP if Froslass survives. Calm Mind is safer: Sucker Punch fails against my status move (no attacking move used), Blizzard is reduced by +1 SpD (~22-32 damage), letting me survive at ~40-50 HP with a +1 SpA boost. Next turn my boosted Dazzling Gleam threatens OHKO on Froslass and severe damage on Kingambit. Kingambit is fainted so I pass; forfeit gives 0% series win probability while fighting on preserves my small chance.
decisions.notebook: Cross-game durable facts confirmed: Foe Kingambit is Adamant Life Orb Defiant with Sucker Punch/Kowtow Cleave; Froslass-Mega is the Snow Warning Blizzard pivot that outspeeds many threats. Foe Sneasler runs Unburden + White Herb Close Combat (off-the-board this game). Foe reserves 1-of-3 unseen: Lycanroc-Dusk/FocusSash/ToughClaws, Basculegion/Adaptability, Scovillain-Mega/Moody. My team identity: Kingambit (Defiant/Blackglasses/Sucker Punch SE on Ghost), Floette-Eternal (Flower Veil ally-protect + Calm Mind pivot, Mega = Fairy Aura offensively). Key lesson: Snow Warning turns are precious — Kingambit frozen in Snowscape cost me game 2 momentum. Future plan game 3: lead with a non-Ice-vulnerable pivot, preserve Kingambit for Sucker Punch on Ghost/Fairy-weak switches, and only commit Floette-Mega offensively into a non-Ice-resist core.

reflections.summary: The Game 2 adjustment helped rather than backfired: Sneasler, Mega Froslass, Kingambit and Basculegion matched up well, and Mega Froslass was the correct evolution. Snow-accurate Blizzard supplied decisive spread pressure, while Sneasler removed Incineroar and the opposing Kingambit. The turn-1 freeze on Kingambit was important luck because it denied multiple actions, but clean, error-free piloting converted that advantage: Froslass also KOed Sneasler and beat Mega Floette. This clinched the authoritative 2-0 series win.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the same Sneasler plus Mega Froslass core and generally the same four; Basculegion was unused but remained a sound reserve. Do not plan around another freeze: proactively use Sneasler to pressure Incineroar and Kingambit, preserve Kingambit as the safest Fairy-resistant Mega Floette answer, and continue exploiting Mega Froslass's guaranteed snow Blizzard and Speed advantage.
reflections.notebook: Opponent has shown a preference for Sneasler plus Incineroar with Kingambit and Mega Floette in back, including willingness to pivot Sneasler immediately into Kingambit while Incineroar pressures Froslass. Mega Froslass at 170 Speed outruns every legal Timid Mega Floette range; Blizzard is fully accurate in snow and dealt about half to Mega Floette. Activated Unburden Sneasler reaches 314 Speed. Kingambit is the safest defensive response to Mega Floette's Fairy attacks. Continue respecting Choice Scarf Basculegion's Speed if it is brought.

reflections.summary: Lost game 2 (and the series 0-2) because my Kingambit froze on the turn-1 Blizzard from opp's Froslass-Mega in Snowscape, immediately neutralizing the one Pokémon on my team built to revenge-kill the Froslass (Sucker Punch) or punish opp's Kingambit pivot (Defiant). With Kingambit frozen I had to bench it turn 2, surrendering tempo to opp's Sneasler, which OHKO'd my Incineroar with Close Combat (4x SE on Fire/Dark) and 2HKO'd my Sneasler with the next Blizzard. My Floette-Mega only entered turn 3, Mega'd turn 4, and its Dazzling Gleam only traded for opp Sneasler — opp Froslass survived at 47% and cleaned my last Pokémon turn 5. Between-game adjustments were insufficient: the stated plan to 'lead non-Ice-vulnerable and preserve Kingambit' was abandoned when I led Sneasler+Incineroar again and pivoted Kingambit in on turn 1, the exact mistake that fed the freeze. The team-preview itself was defensible (the four brought — Sneasler, Kingambit, Incineroar, Floette — were the right tools) but the Mega timing was forced and too late: I had no opportunity to Mega on turns 1-2 and by turn 3 Snow was already established. The series is best read as 'draft correct, sequencing frozen out.'
reflections.adjustment: Lead Floette + Incineroar into opp's Froslass-Mega + Sneasler. Floette-Mega at 169 Spe outspeeds opp's Froslass and OHKOs it with Fairy-Aura Dazzling Gleam in Snowscape before Blizzard can meaningfully chip or freeze my team; Incineroar Intimidate softens opp's Blizzard and Fake Out shuts down opp Sneasler's CC. Mega Floette on turn 1 — do not delay; commit immediately so opp has to respect the Fairy Aura on the spread. Keep Kingambit on the bench: never pivot it into a live Snowscape turn (it is freeze-bait and a single freeze loses the game). Bring Kingambit in only after Snow is down or opp Froslass is dead, as a Defiant revenge-sweeper on opp Kingambit's pivot or as a Sucker-Punch response to a Froslass switch. If the 4th-mon reveal is Scovillain-Mega (Grass/Fire resists Fairy Aura), pivot to Sneasler + Incineroar instead and save Floette-Mega for after Scovillain is chipped.
reflections.notebook:
Confirmed opp profile across the series:
- Kingambit (Adamant Life Orb Defiant; Sucker Punch / Kowtow Cleave / Swords Dance / Protect). Pivots via Protect, revenge-kills Ghosts and Fairies; Kowtow Cleave threatens OHKOs on my Floette-Mega (Dark on Fairy).
- Froslass-Mega (Timid Snow Warning; Blizzard / Shadow Ball / Thunderbolt / Protect). The Snowscape lead and the entire game plan. Blizzard in Snow never misses and hits both opponents; any of my Ice-vulnerable mons that switch in risk freeze, and Steel-types like my Kingambit are especially freeze-bait. My Floette-Mega at 169 Spe outspeeds it.
- Sneasler (Adamant Unburden + White Herb; Fake Out / Close Combat / Dire Claw / Protect). Close Combat is 4x SE on my Incineroar (Fire/Dark) for a clean OHKO; the CC mirror trade also threatens my Sneasler. Has Fake Out priority to disrupt my leads.
- 4th-mon pool (one of): Lycanroc-Dusk (FocusSash ToughClaws; CC / Rock Slide / Accelerock / Protect) — bring Sneasler, CC mirror wins; Basculegion (Adaptability Mystic Water; Last Respects / Aqua Jet / Wave Crash / Protect) — Kingambit Sucker Punch on switch; Scovillain-Mega (Moody) — the dangerous one, Grass/Fire resists Fairy Aura and Moody snowballs, so lead Sucker-Punch Kingambit or Sneasler, NOT Floette.

My team identity (rebuilt from public Regulation M-B sets):
- Kingambit: Defiant / Blackglasses / Sucker Punch — priority revenge-kill on opp Froslass and opp Kingambit; Blackglasses boosts Dark STAB into Ghosts/Psychics. NEVER pivot into Snowscape.
- Floette-Eternal: Mega = Fairy Aura. Dazzling Gleam OHKOs opp Froslass in Snow and threatens opp Sneasler (Fairy on Fighting/Poison). Outspeeds opp Froslass-Mega. Mega on turn 1 in this matchup.
- Sneasler: mirror CC threat, beats Lycanroc-Dusk, threatens opp Kingambit after Defiant boost.
- Incineroar: Intimidate + Fake Out pivot. Intimidate softens opp Blizzard and opp CC; Fake Out shuts down opp Sneasler. Do NOT leave Incineroar exposed without Fake Out support — opp Sneasler CC OHKOs it.

Durable strategic lessons for a rematch:
1. Versus Froslass-Mega Snowscape leads, the correct opener is Floette-Mega + Incineroar to OHKO Froslass before Snow freezes the game.
2. Never pivot Kingambit into a live Snowscape turn — the freeze alone loses tempo and the game.
3. Mega Floette on turn 1 against this comp; delaying forfeits the offensive race against Snow chip.
4. Save Kingambit as a mid/late-game revenge-sweeper on opp Kingambit or as a Sucker-Punch response once Snow is down or Froslass is dead.
5. Opp Sneasler OHKOs Incineroar with CC — pair Incineroar with Fake Out support or pivot out on Sneasler reveal.

decisions.rationale: Staraptor+Raichu lead gives Intimidate+Fake Out+Tailwind vs Whimsicott/Charizard sun; Raichu Mega Mega Guard Zap-G Zap Dragon  KO cover vs Basculegion/Charizard/Kingambit, Sylveon Pixilate Hyper Voice is only 2x vs Garchomp (Raichu Electric immune) and spread pressure, Arcanine-Hisui Rock Head Head Smash 4x OHKO Charizard-Y and resists Heat Wave + Flare Blitz vs Whimsicott/Floette/Kingambit + Extreme Speed. Covers all 6 opponent threats; Kingambit/Farigiraf less essential than Fire/Rock resist and Fairy spread.
decisions.notebook: Opp 6: Charizard-Y Drought sun Heat Wave/SolarBeam, Whimsicott Prankster Tailwind/Encore, Garchomp LO Jolly, Basculegion Adaptability Mystic Water WaveCrash/AquaJet, Floette-Eternal Floettite Fairy, Kingambit Chople Defiant. Opp has two megas Y/Floette. Our megas Staraptor Contrary CC (+Def/SpD) and Raichu-Y No Guard ZapCannon 100% para + Focus Blast. Plan: Tailwind vs Tailwind, Fake Out Whimsicott, Head Smash Charizard, Hyper Voice vs Garchomp, Electric vs Basculegion. Keep Armor Tail/TR in mind for later games if they lean priority.

decisions.rationale: Their team is Normal/Fighting/Fairy/Dark-heavy, so Floette-Eternal (mega it for Fairy Aura) is a near-perfect defensive and offensive pick: it resists Fighting (Close Combat/Focus Blast), Dark (Kowtow/Sucker Punch) and Fairy (Pixilate Hyper Voice), is immune to Dragon, and Fairy-Aura Light of Ruin nukes both Mega Staraptor and Kingambit. Garchomp pairs with it for fast Ground/Rock coverage (4x on Hisuian Arcanine, super-effective on Kingambit and Raichu, Rock Slide into Staraptor) and to help remove Farigiraf before Trick Room (-7) resolves. Backs: Basculegion, which is outright immune to every Normal move (Fake Out, Extreme Speed, Quick Attack, Hyper Beam) and every Fighting move on their sheet while Adaptability Wave Crash is 4x on Arcanine; and Whimsicott for Prankster Tailwind to answer Staraptor's Tailwind plus Encore/Protect utility. Charizard is left home because Hisuian Arcanine's Head Smash is 4x and Raichu's No-Guard Zap Cannon is 2x on it, and its sun would boost their Flare Blitz; only one mega can evolve anyway.
decisions.notebook:
OPP (Reg M-B, open sheets): Staraptor @Staraptite (Jolly, Intimidate; Tailwind/Protect/CloseCombat/DualWingbeat; Mega = Fighting/Flying, CONTRARY so Close Combat RAISES its Def/SpD - do not let it snowball, kill with Fairy/Rock/Psychic); Raichu @RaichuniteY (Timid, LightningRod; FakeOut/ZapCannon/FocusBlast/Protect; Mega-Y = No Guard so Zap Cannon 120 NEVER misses and always paralyzes, Focus Blast never misses - my Ghost (Basculegion) is immune to Focus Blast, Ground (Garchomp) immune to Zap Cannon); Sylveon @FairyFeather (Modest, Pixilate: HyperVoice/HyperBeam/QuickAttack are FAIRY-typed spread/priority; Detect); Farigiraf @SitrusBerry (Calm, ARMOR TAIL = my priority moves targeting their side fail, so Whimsicott Encore/Prankster Encore and Kingambit Sucker Punch/Aqua Jet do NOTHING while Farigiraf is on field; carries Trick Room, Helping Hand, Psychic); Arcanine-Hisui @FocusSash (Jolly, RockHead: HeadSmash 150 no recoil, FlareBlitz, ExtremeSpeed +2, Protect) - needs 2 hits through Sash; Kingambit @LifeOrb (Adamant, Defiant, SwordsDance/KowtowCleave/SuckerPunch/Protect) - never lower its stats (Intimidate-style), beware SD snowball, my Fairy/Ground/Fire hit it.
MY TEAM notes: only ONE mega may evolve per game; Floette-Eternal @Floettite -> Fairy Aura (base 155 SpA, Spe 102 base) is the premier mega vs this team; Charizard @CharizarditeY is the alternative but is 4x weak to Head Smash and 2x to Zap Cannon and its sun powers their Flare Blitz. Paralysed Floette (77 Spe) is nearly dead weight - keep it out of Zap Cannon range; G2/G3 lead Whimsicott + Basculegion, Mega Floette later. Basculegion is immune to Normal (ExtremeSpeed, HyperVoice-if-not-Pixilate, CloseCombat is Fighting so it does hit... CloseCombat neutral) - true Normal moves cannot touch it, and Ghost moves do nothing to Staraptor/Farigiraf. Race Farigiraf before Trick Room; slow Basculegion is fine under TR.

decisions.rationale: Both actives fainted; Mega Floette is my last Pokemon and must be brought in. Slot placement is irrelevant in doubles here since both foes are adjacent to either slot. Next turn plan: Dazzling Gleam is a spread hit that removes Arcanine-Hisui at 1% HP even at 0.5x and chips Sylveon; Light of Ruin (Fairy Aura boosted) is the single-target nuke if I need max damage on Sylveon, though Fairy is resisted by it. Paralysis makes Floette slower than Sylveon, so it will likely eat Hyper Voice first.
decisions.notebook:
OPP TEAM (Reg M-B, open sheets): Staraptor @Staraptite (Jolly, Intimidate; Tailwind/Protect/CloseCombat/DualWingbeat; Mega = Fighting/Flying CONTRARY, so its Close Combat RAISES its Def/SpD). Raichu @RaichuniteY (Timid; Mega-Y No Guard Zap Cannon = guaranteed para, ~50% on Mega Floette). Sylveon @FairyFeather (Modest, Pixilate: Hyper Voice/Hyper Beam/Quick Attack all become FAIRY; Hyper Voice is a spread nuke and the single biggest threat on their team; Detect). Farigiraf @SitrusBerry (Calm, Armor Tail blocks priority aimed at their side; my self-targeting Protect/Tailwind still work). Arcanine-Hisui @FocusSash (Jolly, Rock Head Head Smash 150, Extreme Speed +2, Flare Blitz). Kingambit @LifeOrb (Adamant, Defiant - never lower its stats, avoid Intimidate-style effects). MY DAMAGE REFS: Basculegion (Adamant @MysticWater, Adaptability): Aqua Jet 99-188% vs Arcanine-Hisui (4x, +1 priority, pops Sash), Wave Crash 293-546% vs Arcanine, Wave Crash 83-160% vs Sylveon, Last Respects 28-56% vs Sylveon at 1 fainted ally (+50 BP per extra fainted ally - late-game it one-shots most of their team). Aqua Jet OHKOs weakened Staraptor. Whimsicott Moonblast only 13-24% vs Arcanine. Mega Floette (Modest, Fairy Aura): Dazzling Gleam spread; Fairy is 0.5x into Arcanine-Hisui and into Sylveon, so Floette is a poor answer to both - Basculegion is the Arcanine/Sylveon answer.
KEY LESSONS FOR G2/G3: (1) Sylveon Pixilate Hyper Voice is their engine - it crit-KOd Whimsicott through Sash chip and 2HKOs almost everything I have. Lead to pressure Sylveon immediately or bring a Steel/Poison-resist answer; Basculegion Wave Crash is my cleanest Sylveon KO. (2) Focus Sash mons need two separate hits; chip damage does not bypass Sash. (3) Do not let Mega Floette get paralysed - paralysed Floette (~77 Spe) is dead weight; keep it off the field while Raichu-Y (No Guard Zap Cannon) is alive. (4) Basculegion is immune to true Normal moves (Extreme Speed / non-Pixilate Hyper Voice) but Pixilate makes Sylveon's Normal moves Fairy and thus super effective-neutral, and Close Combat (Fighting) hits it normally. Ghost moves do nothing to Staraptor/Farigiraf. (5) Race Farigiraf before Trick Room; slow Basculegion is actually fine under TR. (6) Whimsicott Prankster Tailwind is only worth it if a body will survive to profit from it; against Extreme Speed/Quick Attack chip, Whimsicott dies fast. (7) Preferred G2/G3 bring: Basculegion + Whimsicott lead with Floette and a bulkier partner in back; use Encore on Protect/Tailwind users and Aqua Jet to snipe Sash/weakened Fire-Rock and Flying threats.

decisions.rationale: Flare Blitz (45.3-84.6%) + Pixilate Hyper Voice (33.1-57% spread) min 78.4% >47% guarantees KO on Floette-Mega with two 100% accurate moves before it acts (Arcanine 156 and Sylveon 95 > paralyzed Floette 61-77). reflections.summary: Won Game 2 (6 turns) and series 2-0 with clean piloting (0 errors). Preview plan suited opponent's actual 4: they benched Whimsicott (Prankster Tailwind/Encore) and Floette-Eternal (Mega Fairy) and brought Charizard-Mega-Y/Garchomp/Basculegion/Kingambit. Our 4 - Staraptor (Tailwind/Intimidate) + Raichu (Fake Out/Lightning Rod) + Sylveon (Pixilate Hyper Voice) + Arcanine-H (Rock Head Head Smash/Extreme Speed/Sash) - directly answered that: Tailwind vs sun, Fake Out vs Garchomp Rock Slide, spread Hyper Voice super-effective vs Garchomp and chunking Kingambit/Basculegion, Head Smash super-effective vs Charizard-Y and Extreme Speed for Kingambit. Mega choice was correct: neither Staraptorite nor Raichunite-Y was evolved - base utility (Intimidate, Fake Out, speed) mattered more than Mega power and preserved tempo. Piloting executed plan: T1 Fake Out flinch Garchomp secured Tailwind despite Staraptor lost to Heat Wave, T2 pivot Sylveon for Arcanine, T3-5 Hyper Voice spread + Protect + Extreme Speed cleaned Garchomp/Kingambit/Basculegion, T6 Head Smash finished re-entered Charizard-Y. Series win = favorable preview matchup + error-free tempo control; no between-game adjustment backfired (1-0 lead held).
reflections.adjustment: No major change needed vs this Charizard-Y sun + Garchomp/Kingambit/Basculegion offense - keep same 4 and keep Mega unevolved for utility. In a future series expect opponent to re-introduce benched Whimsicott Tailwind war and Floette-Eternal Mega Fairy (Light of Ruin) - if so, prioritize keeping Arcanine-H Sash intact for Fairy/Charizard and consider Sylveon + Raichu lead to pressure Fairy while still contesting Tailwind, don't force early Mega evolution.
reflections.notebook: Top-cut sun offense player. Tendency: lead Charizard-Y + Garchomp, Mega evolve Charizard T1 to set sun, play Heat Wave spread + Protect stall, Garchomp Rock Slide spread. Backline is Kingambit (Chople, Sucker Punch) + Basculegion (Adaptability Aqua Jet) for priority cleanup. Willing to bench usual Prankster Whimsicott Tailwind/Encore and Floette-Eternal Mega Fairy to go 4 attackers vs Tailwind/Fake Out teams (did so in G2). Counter durable: Fake Out Garchomp to guarantee Tailwind, Pixilate Hyper Voice pressures entire core, Extreme Speed answers low Kingambit through Sucker Punch, Rock Head Head Smash answers Charizard-Y without Sash break.

reflections.summary: Lost the game and the series to the same pattern as Game 1: I traded pieces one-at-a-time and ended up in a 1-vs-2. The preview plan was half-right — Mega Charizard-Y's turn-1 Heat Wave again cleanly removed Staraptor before it could Mega (denying Contrary Close Combat) and chipped Raichu to 7% — but the other three brought (Garchomp, Basculegion, Kingambit) all matched up badly into the surviving backline. Garchomp's Rock Slide missed the Focus-Sash Arcanine-Hisui on turn 2, so the sash never broke and Arcanine stayed a full-power Head Smash threat all game; Garchomp then died to Sylveon's Pixilate Hyper Voice (Life Orb chip + spread Fairy). Kingambit was dead weight for the third time: at 81 Speed it only ever gets Sucker Punch, which failed into Arcanine's Protect, and it absorbed two Hyper Voices before dying to a resisted Extreme Speed. Basculegion, my one real Arcanine answer, had its Aqua Jet halved by my own Drought, so it needed two turns to get Arcanine to 25% and was picked off by Hyper Beam first. That left a lone Mega Zard forced in against a healthy-enough Arcanine, which auto-OHKOs it with Head Smash — the loss was locked in a turn before it happened. Piloting was clean on paper (0 errors, correct Protect on the Head Smash turn), but the structural errors were team-level: two Fairy-vulnerable slow bodies, and a sun setter that actively weakens the Water attacker I needed. The between-game adjustment (same lead, Kingambit brought again) did not help and effectively backfired — it repeated the exact Game 1 failure mode.
reflections.adjustment: Bench Kingambit entirely — it has now been a non-factor in every game and only feeds Sylveon's spread Fairy damage. Bring a fourth that can pressure Arcanine-Hisui and Sylveon without fighting my own sun, and stop pairing two Fairy-weak/slow bodies with Sylveon on the field. Keep Mega Charizard-Y purely as a turn-1 tool: Heat Wave to remove Staraptor before it Megas and chip Raichu, then get it off the field immediately and never let it end up as the last mon, since Arcanine outspeeds it and Head Smash is a guaranteed OHKO. Answer Arcanine with Solar Beam/Ground damage rather than sun-halved Water, and when Basculegion is needed as the Water answer, either delay Mega evolution or accept that Aqua Jet needs a chip partner. Break the Focus Sash and finish in the same turn — spread damage first, single-target kill second — instead of chipping across turns and letting Protect reset tempo. Above all, stop the greedy single-target trade pattern: preserve two healthy bodies through the Tailwind turns and let their Tailwind expire (it ran out on turn 4 both times) before committing to KO attempts.

OPP TEAM (Reg M-B, open sheets): Staraptor @Staraptite (Jolly, Intimidate; Tailwind/Protect/CloseCombat/DualWingbeat; Mega = Fighting/Flying CONTRARY). Raichu @RaichuniteY (Timid; Fake Out/ZapCannon/FocusBlast/Protect; Mega-Y No Guard Zap Cannon = guaranteed para). Farigiraf @SitrusBerry (Calm, Armor Tail blocks priority on their side). Kingambit @LifeOrb (Adamant, Defiant, SwordsDance/KowtowCleave/SuckerPunch/Protect).

DURABLE TENDENCIES (3 games observed): Leads Staraptor + Raichu every single game — never deviated. Backline has always been Sylveon + Arcanine-Hisui; Farigiraf and their Kingambit have NEVER been brought (but assume Trick Room/Armor Tail is possible in a fresh series and never rely solely on priority). Turn 1 they commit Staraptor to Tailwind rather than Protect, even into an obvious Fire lead — Staraptor is expendable and has died turn 1 repeatedly without ever Mega evolving. Raichu's Fake Out targets my physical attacker, not the special threat, and Raichu has never actually Mega evolved yet. Arcanine-Hisui spams Head Smash freely (Rock Head, no recoil) and uses Protect on turns where a priority/Water attack is obvious. Sylveon will fire Hyper Beam to guarantee a KO and accept the recharge — that recharge turn is a free turn for me. Their Tailwind expires after turn 4; games are decided by whether I still have two healthy bodies at that point.

SPEED/THREAT FACTS: Arcanine-H (raw 121-156) outspeeds Mega Zard (135). Mega Raichu (165-200) outspeeds my entire team. Intimidate on the Staraptor lead drops both my physical leads a stage.

DAMAGE (sun): Arcanine-H Head Smash — Mega Zard 226-331% (auto OHKO), Basculegion 60-87%, Kingambit 16-34%; Flare Blitz OHKOs Kingambit from full; Extreme Speed — Basculegion IMMUNE (Ghost), Kingambit 0.5x. Sylveon Hyper Voice (spread Fairy) — Kingambit 38-55%, Basculegion 41-59%; Hyper Beam OHKOs a ~half-HP Basculegion. Raichu Zap Cannon — Mega Zard 65-97%; Focus Blast — Kingambit 72-167%.
MY NUMBERS (sun): Mega Zard Heat Wave OHKOs Staraptor from full and chips Raichu heavily; Heat Wave into Arcanine only 12-22% (0.25x); Solar Beam into Arcanine 36-66% (neutral, instant in sun); sun Weather Ball = 100BP Fire, best neutral single-target nuke. Basculegion Aqua Jet into Arcanine-H 47.5-94% (halved by my own sun). Kingambit Iron Head into Sylveon 78-152%, Sucker Punch into Arcanine 30-57%.

STANDING LESSONS: (1) Mega Zard must never share the field with a healthy Arcanine-Hisui and must never be the last mon — Head Smash is a guaranteed OHKO. (2) Removing Raichu/Staraptor turn 1 with Heat Wave works, but killing the lead is not enough; the Sylveon + Arcanine back pair is what actually wins their games. (3) My own Drought halves my Water moves — the Zard/Basculegion pairing is anti-synergistic against the mon Water is meant to answer. (4) Focus Sash is dead once chipped: chip and finish inside the same turn. (5) Kingambit (81 Spe) has contributed nothing in three games — Sucker Punch fails into Protect/Arcanine's non-attacking turns, and it just eats Hyper Voice; bench it. (6) Every loss came from collapsing into a 1-vs-2+; trade evenly, survive Tailwind, avoid stacking Fairy-vulnerable bodies against Sylveon.

decisions.rationale: Lead Sneasler+Incineroar: double Fake Out wins the flinch war (their only Fake Out is Sneasler, max 172 < my 189), Intimidate blunts their four physical attackers, and Quick Guard blocks all their priority (Fake Out/Accelerock/Aqua Jet/Sucker Punch). Back Kingambit resists both Mega Froslass's and Basculegion's STABs and OHKOs Froslass even in snow; Mega Delphox at 204 Speed outspeeds their entire team, with Psyshock 4x vs Sneasler and Heat Wave 2x vs Kingambit/Froslass. Blastoise's Water Spout is resisted by 4 of their 6 and Sinistcha is 2x weak to Blizzard, so both sit out.
decisions.notebook: Opponent team: physical-heavy (Sneasler/Lycanroc/Basculegion/Kingambit) with Mega Froslass snow-Blizzard or Mega Scovillain as mega choice; their ONLY Fake Out user is Sneasler (Adamant, <=172 Spe, White Herb+Unburden). My key answers: my Sneasler (189) outspeeds theirs; Close Combat 4x vs their Kingambit. My Kingambit resists Froslass and Basculegion STABs; Kowtow Cleave OHKOs Mega Froslass even under snow Def boost; Sucker Punch endgame. My Mega Delphox hits 204 Spe, outspeeding everything incl. Mega Froslass (<=189); Psyshock 4x vs Sneasler, Heat Wave 2x vs Froslass/Kingambit (snow halves Fire dmg, so Froslass survives one Heat Wave in snow). Quick Guard (Sneasler) blocks their Fake Out, Accelerock, Aqua Jet, Sucker Punch. Dangers to remember: Delphox is 2x weak to Sucker Punch/Accelerock/Aqua Jet/Shadow Ball; my Kingambit is 4x weak to their Close Combats (Sneasler, Lycanroc); their Basculegion Last Respects snowballs as KOs happen, and Scovillain can Rage Powder to enable Blizzard. Plan for series: open Sneasler+Incineroar for Fake Out control + Intimidate, keep Kingambit+Delphox as cleaners; adapt lead if they repeatedly open Rage Powder+Blizzard.

decisions.rationale: Lead Sneasler plus Froslass for Fake Out pressure, an opposing Fake Out immunity, and broad fast coverage. Kingambit covers Sinistcha and Delphox while discouraging Incineroar’s Intimidate and Parting Shot; Basculegion gives the strongest late-game answer to the Fire-types and benefits from fallen allies powering Last Respects.
decisions.notebook: Game-plan baseline: prioritize Mega Froslass for Snow Warning and fast Blizzard pressure. Preserve Sneasler to threaten opposing Kingambit and Blastoise, Kingambit to punish Intimidate/Parting Shot and pressure Sinistcha, and Basculegion for late-game cleanup against Incineroar and Delphox. Scout opposing Sneasler’s Speed relative to Mega Froslass and our Sneasler.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out into their Sneasler is my only way to punish its likely Close Combat/Dire Claw into Incineroar (its CC is a near-OHKO on Incineroar): my +3 Fake Out beats its 0-priority attacks and flinches it, and the only counter is their own faster Unburden Fake Out, which just trades chip. Flare Blitz into Froslass threatens an OHKO (2x, ~OHKO even vs Mega in snow) before it can start a snow-Blizzard loop; Froslass is Ghost-immune to both my Fake Outs, so damage is the only way to remove it, and worst case it Protects or wastes a turn while Blizzard only tickles Incineroar (0.5x, Sitrus behind). Quick Guard is useless here since their Sneasler outspeeds inside the +3 bracket.
decisions.notebook: Opponent team: physical-heavy (Sneasler/Lycanroc/Basculegion/Kingambit) with Mega Froslass snow-Blizzard or Mega Scovillain as mega choice; their only Fake Out user is Sneasler (Adamant). Game 1: they lead Sneasler+Froslass, 2 more unseen. Foe Sneasler: White Herb already consumed by my Intimidate -> Unburden active (280-344 Spe, outspeeds everything I have incl. Mega Delphox), itemless now, neutral Atk; its CC (~182 Adamant Atk) near-OHKOs my Incineroar (2x) and 4x-KOs my Kingambit - never leave either exposed to it. My Sneasler resists both its STABs and holds Focus Sash; Mega Delphox Psyshock is 4x OHKO on it. Froslass: immune to Fake Out; if it Megas, snow's Ice Def boost still leaves it in Flare Blitz/Kowtow Cleave KO range; Kingambit walls it (resists Blizzard + Shadow Ball). Quick Guard cannot beat their faster Fake Out - only use vs their priority once Sneasler is gone (Accelerock/Aqua Jet/Sucker Punch). Plan: preserve my Sneasler sash as their-Sneasler check, kill Froslass via Incineroar/Kingambit, then clean with Mega Delphox (204 Spe) + Kingambit Sucker Punch. Watch: Basculegion Last Respects snowball after KOs; Scovillain Rage Powder could redirect my Froslass kill.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out stops Incineroar from immediately threatening Froslass, while Mega Evolution sets snow and makes Blizzard accurate for spread damage. Our Unburden Sneasler acts before both opposing Fake Out users, so Quick Guard cannot retroactively stop this Fake Out.

Preserve Sneasler for opposing Kingambit and Blastoise, Kingambit to punish Intimidate or Parting Shot and pressure Sinistcha, and Basculegion for late-game cleanup against Incineroar and Delphox. decisions.rationale: My Sneasler (41%, sash already broken) is guaranteed dead to Blizzard and cannot be saved, so it stays as fodder and fires Close Combat into their Sneasler (~29-59% chip) to drag it toward Kingambit Sucker Punch range (~38-45%) — Poison Jab chip would leave it too healthy. Incineroar is a guaranteed KO to their Sneasler's Close Combat if it stays (77.6-111.4%), so it pivots out: Kingambit can never switch in (CC is a 4x guaranteed OHKO), while Delphox tanks CC (0.5x, ~50-60%) plus Blizzard (0.5x, ~20-29%) and threatens a 4x Psyshock OHKO (239-285%) on their Sneasler. Next turn Kingambit comes in on the fainted Sneasler and Sucker Punch cleans up their chipped Sneasler if it attacks, with Delphox Psyshock as the other kill route; Kingambit then walls Froslass and KOs it with Kowtow Cleave.
decisions.notebook: Opponent team: physical-heavy (Sneasler/Lycanroc/Basculegion/Kingambit) with Mega Froslass snow-Blizzard or Mega Scovillain as mega choice; their only Fake Out user is Sneasler (Adamant, Unburden, White Herb).
