Watch: Basculegion Last Respects snowball after KOs, Scovillain Rage Powder redirecting my Froslass kill, Lycanroc Accelerock picking off low-HP mons. Mega Delphox timing: Mega when a safe turn appears for the SpA boost; verify Mega Speed with compare_action_order before relying on outspeeding Froslass (non-Mega 171 already beats low-roll Froslass).

decisions.rationale: Kingambit is the safe replacement: it resists everything Froslass-Mega has (Blizzard, Shadow Ball, Thunderbolt), and its Life Orb Sucker Punch (+1 priority) KOs the 20% Sneasler before it can move if it attacks, neutralizing the 4x Close Combat threat — their Sneasler also already burned its only Fake Out. I deliberately do NOT Mega this turn: Blaze is active at 29% HP, and Blaze-boosted non-Mega Heat Wave (~249 effective SpA) out-damages Mega Delphox (211 SpA) — Mega's only real gain is 204 Speed to guarantee outspeeding Froslass (189 max), but Kingambit alone controls Froslass (Kowtow Cleave 75-141%, plus Sucker Punch pressure), and I can Mega on any later attack turn if that speed guarantee becomes necessary. decisions.rationale: It's a 2v1 endgame: their only remaining Pokemon is Kingambit at 96%/+1. Double-target it: my Kowtow Cleave (~20-30% resisted chip) plus Incineroar's Flare Blitz (~64-75%) totals ~84-105%, frequently KOing outright. Even if they Protect, Sucker Punch, or KO my 31% Kingambit with Kowtow, Incineroar resists all their Dark STAB, still holds Sitrus, and guaranteed-2HKOs them while they cannot KO Incineroar through resist+Sitrus before the second Flare Blitz lands. Parting Shot would fail with no benched ally, and Sucker Punch risks failing into Protect/Swords Dance, so Kowtow is the higher-EV chip.
decisions.notebook: Confirmed calcs (Game 1): my LO Kingambit Sucker Punch guaranteed-KOs their Sneasler from >=20% and outprioritizes CC. Kowtow Cleave vs Froslass-Mega through snow = 75-141%. Delphox Heat Wave + Kowtow = guaranteed Froslass KO; Froslass Shadow Ball KOs Delphox from <=29%. Basculegion Wave Crash vs my Incineroar = guaranteed KO from 70% EVEN at -1 Atk; NEVER let Incineroar take one; Basculegion (98-130 Spe) always outspeeds Incineroar (88), so Incineroar needs Fake Out priority for guaranteed value. Aqua Jet vs Incineroar ~25-37% at -1 (survives, Sitrus). My +0 LO Kingambit vs Basculegion: Sucker Punch 73-137%, Kowtow 87-168%. Incineroar Throat Chop vs Basculegion 46-87%; Flare Blitz vs Kingambit-bulk ~64-75% (2HKO). Foe +1 LO Kowtow vs my Kingambit ~30-39% of max (KOs from <=31%, not from 41%); +1 Sucker ~25-32% (coin-flip from 31%). Their Kingambit's Speed remains unknown within 70-102 (never saw it move unflinched vs my 71). Endgame pattern proven: 2v1 vs their Kingambit, double-target with Kowtow chip + Flare Blitz; their Dark STAB is resisted by Incineroar and Sitrus+resist means they can't race the 2HKO. Parting Shot fails with no alive benched ally — never click it in a 2v1 endgame. Backline threats for later games: Lycanroc-Dusk Tough Claws CC 4x vs Kingambit (answer: Intimidate + Flare Blitz/Sucker); Scovillain Overheat 2x vs Kingambit, Rage Powder redirects. Their Sneasler: Unburden persists after White Herb; answer with Sucker Punch/Protect only. Delphox is max-Speed Timid (171; Mega 204 beats max Froslass 189); Mega forfeits Blaze — Mega only to outspeed Froslass or for Levitate.

decisions.rationale: Protect blocks the likely double attack and can force opposing Life Orb Kingambit to lose HP, putting it into a more reliable Sucker Punch KO range next turn. Attacking now risks being finished by Incineroar’s faster Flare Blitz plus opposing Kingambit.
decisions.notebook: Prioritize Mega Froslass for Snow Warning and Blizzard pressure. Kingambit punishes Intimidate and Parting Shot through Defiant. Basculegion is the preferred late-game cleaner into Incineroar and Delphox. Basculegion Aqua Jet guarantees a KO on Delphox from 29%. At -1 Attack, Basculegion Wave Crash deals 37.7-64% to opposing Kingambit and 83.2-150.6% to Incineroar. Opposing Kingambit's Sucker Punch deals 91.8-131.9% to Basculegion and 75.5-111% to Mega Froslass. Mega Froslass Thunderbolt deals 22.7-41.7% to opposing Kingambit. At +1 Attack, allied Kingambit Sucker Punch deals 20.8-34.9% and Kowtow Cleave deals 24.6-42.3% to opposing Kingambit. Opposing Incineroar is guaranteed faster than allied Kingambit and Flare Blitz deals 63.8-92.8% to it.

decisions.rationale: 2v1 endgame: double-target their last Pokémon. Incineroar Flare Blitz does 63.8-75.4% (SE) and my Kowtow Cleave adds 16.4-28% chip, summing 80-103% — often a clean KO from 96%, and always leaving them in range of next turn's Flare Blitz. I choose Kowtow over Sucker Punch because Sucker fails if they click Swords Dance (or Protect), and the Kowtow chip specifically closes the +3 Sucker-Punch race; even if their +1 Kowtow KOs my Kingambit first (only a high-roll KO from 31%), Incineroar resists Dark (their +1 Sucker does just 22-33%), has Sitrus intact, and wins the 2HKO race alone. All branches end with their Kingambit fainting to Flare Blitz.

decisions.rationale: Sucker Punch into opposing Kingambit gives the best immediate win chance by potentially KOing it before it attacks; Kingambit can then survive Incineroar's non-critical Flare Blitz and retain a narrow endgame chance.

reflections.summary: Preview plan was sound: Sneasler/Incineroar/Kingambit/Delphox covered everything they brought, and the Kingambit + Incineroar core won the game — Sucker Punch removed their Sneasler and Basculegion, Kowtow Cleave one-shot Mega Froslass from full through snow, and in the 2v1 endgame double-targeting Kowtow + Flare Blitz broke their Kingambit's Protect/Sucker pattern, with a Flare Blitz burn sealing the trade. The shaky parts were piloting, not the plan: turn 1 let their faster Sneasler + instant Mega Froslass double Fake Out + Blizzard flinch Incineroar and chunk my Sneasler, and Mega Delphox was wasted — it Mega'd straight into Basculegion's Aqua Jet and never moved. Delphox as the Mega holder was fine on paper (204 Speed beats Froslass), but the timing gained nothing.
reflections.adjustment: Against their standard Sneasler + Mega Froslass opener, click Quick Guard with Sneasler on turn 1: their Sneasler outspeeds my 189 Jolly one, so I lose the Fake Out race, but Quick Guard blocks both Fake Outs, keeps Incineroar unflinched, and frees it to Flare Blitz Froslass-Mega super effectively (leading Kingambit, which resists Blizzard/Shadow Ball and shrugs off Fake Out, is the fallback). Separately, only Mega Delphox when it flips a same-turn interaction — never into a live Basculegion, whose Aqua Jet priority ignores the 204 Speed.

The game was lost in the endgame because opposing Kingambit immediately removed Basculegion with Sucker Punch while Incineroar’s Fake Out and faster Flare Blitz neutralized allied Kingambit, leaving no remaining answer to their physical core.

decisions.rationale: Run back the G1-winning structure: lead Sneasler + Incineroar, back Kingambit + Delphox. Their Sneasler's raw Speed cap is 172, so it cannot actually outspeed my 189 Sneasler — G1 it only moved first via Fake Out priority. That means at equal +3 priority my Quick Guard resolves BEFORE their Fake Out, so turn 1 Quick Guard blocks Fake Out side-wide, Intimidate drops their physical attackers, and Incineroar is free to Flare Blitz Froslass (or their Sneasler if Froslass Protects). The one bad matchup is a Basculegion lead since Incineroar lacks Protect; contingency is Fake Out Basculegion + Flare Blitz Froslass, then clean with Kingambit's Sucker Punch/Kowtow (73-168% range) and Delphox. Kingambit answers Froslass (Kowtow OHKO range), Sneasler (Sucker from 20%), and Basculegion; Delphox gives 171-Speed control with Psyshock 4x into Sneasler and Heat Wave into Froslass. Same four as the G1 win; re-evaluate for G3 only if they anti-lead successfully.

Tendencies: G1 lead Sneasler+Froslass (instant Mega); G2 lead Kingambit+Sneasler, Kingambit Protected t1; they pivot Kingambit to Ghosts vs CC — cover with Flare Blitz; my Throat Chop is SE into both Ghosts. G3 swap options: Delphox->Sinistcha (immune CC/Fake Out, Rage Powder shields Kingambit, Trick Room) or Blastoise (resists Basculegion's Water).

Aqua Jet acts before Sucker Punch and, together with Thunderbolt, guarantees the Incineroar KO if Froslass gets to move. decisions.rationale: Delphox must Protect while Mega Evolving: Wave Crash is a guaranteed OHKO on it (225-328%) and Shadow Ball can OHKO non-Mega; Mega's SpD lets it survive Shadow Ball and its 204 Speed outspeeds Froslass-Mega (max 189) for next turn. Kingambit Sucker Punches Basculegion: +1 priority strikes before Wave Crash/Last Respects with a ~58% OHKO (73-137%), and it is the only move that contests their guaranteed-kill line of Wave Crash + Thunderbolt on Kingambit from 72% (75.8-110.6%) by removing Basculegion first. Kowtow Cleave (84% KO) was considered but Basculegion moves first against it, making the double-target on Kingambit fatal ~100%. I accept Sucker whiffing versus Aqua Jet/Protect — Aqua Jet + Thunderbolt only chips Kingambit to ~14-33%, it survives, keeps Protect fresh, and Delphox comes online as Mega.
decisions.notebook: Series 1-0 (G2). Sim mechanics confirmed: Sucker Punch FAILS if the target already moved (seen t3/t5) — blank vs faster priority (Basculegion Aqua Jet) and vs Protect/switch-in; works vs 0-priority attackers regardless of their Speed. Kowtow Cleave never misses. Confirmed calcs: my Sucker->Basculegion 73-137% (~58% OHKO), Kowtow->Basc 87-168% (~84%), Sucker->Froslass 62-119%; Basc Wave Crash = guaranteed OHKO on Delphox (even Mega), 54-80% vs my Kingambit, Aqua Jet->King 18-28%; Froslass Tbolt->King 22-30% (WC+Tbolt = guaranteed KO on King from 72%); Froslass Shadow Ball->Mega Delphox ~66-95% (survives), ->non-Mega 80-115%; Mega Delphox Heat Wave->Froslass only ~62-116% (~30% OHKO, unreliable), ->Basc resisted 15-27%; Psyshock->Basc ~42-47%. Mega Delphox 204 Spe > Froslass max 189, but < Unburden Sneasler (280-344); Sneasler CC KOs Delphox, Kingambit Sucker KOs low Sneasler — Kingambit is the answer to both Basculegion and Sneasler, preserve it; if either of my mons dies the endgame collapses (Delphox can't beat Basculegion, King can't 1v3). Opponent tendencies: double-targets the immediate threat (t5 AJ+Tbolt), Protects to scout (their King t1, Froslass t4), pivots Kingambit to Ghosts vs CC; they have SEEN Sucker fail to Aqua Jet so may lean on AJ/Protect as Sucker-counters — mix in Kowtow to punish. G3 swap ideas: Delphox->Sinistcha (immune CC/Fake Out, Rage Powder shields King, Trick Room) or Blastoise (resists Basc Water); never Intimidate their Defiant Kingambit.

decisions.rationale: Protect shields Froslass from Kingambit's likely Sucker Punch and Delphox's pressure, while Aqua Jet resolves before Sucker Punch and safely deals major super-effective damage to Delphox with a possible OHKO. This preserves Froslass and ensures Basculegion contributes before potentially being hit, while keeping Sneasler available to finish Kingambit.

Opposing Kingambit's Life Orb Sucker Punch has only a possible OHKO on full-health Mega Froslass or Basculegion.

decisions.rationale: Both foes outspeed Kingambit, so Sucker Punch is guaranteed to fail; Kowtow Cleave must go into Basculegion — it's their win-condition mon (beats both of mine) and my ~84% OHKO target. Delphox is certain to eat Wave Crash (guaranteed OHKO) since it's the obvious reduced-Protect target and my only Sneasler answer, so it must gamble on the ~1/3 Protect; if it holds and Kowtow connects, the game flips to my favor with King's Protect still fresh for next turn. Attacking with Delphox concedes their most likely line for nothing, and Protecting King instead only pays if they double into a fresh Protect, which this opponent is too disciplined to do.

Calcs: Kowtow(+1)->Basculegion 87-168% (~84% OHKO); Kowtow->Froslass ~75-144%; Basc Wave Crash = guaranteed OHKO on Mega Delphox, 54-80% vs my King; WC+Tbolt guaranteed KO on King from ~72%; Froslass SB->Mega Delphox 66-95%; snow Blizzard only ~20% chip (NVE both); Heat Wave->Froslass 62-116% (~30% OHKO), ->Basc 15-27%; Psyshock 4x vs Sneasler = KO from 16%; Sneasler CC 4x vs King = OHKO but only ~46% vs Mega Delphox; Unburden Sneasler 280-344 Spe > Mega Delphox 204 > Froslass max 189. Their Sneasler still has Fake Out for its re-entry turn (can flinch Delphox — when it just switched in, Protect Delphox, attack with King). Core: King is my ONLY Basculegion answer (Kowtow), Delphox my ONLY Sneasler answer (Psyshock) — if either falls, the rest clean up; always Kowtow Basc, never Froslass. Opponent: double-targets the immediate threat, respects fresh Protect (scouts/pivots), but fires into a burned Protect — expect the lethal move into any slot whose Protect is reduced. They lean on Aqua Jet/Protect as Sucker-counters; Kowtow punishes. G3 swap ideas: Delphox->Sinistcha (immune CC/Fake Out, Rage Powder shields King, Trick Room) or Blastoise (resists Basc Water); never Intimidate their Defiant Kingambit.

decisions.rationale: Double-target Delphox-Mega with Aqua Jet and Shadow Ball. Aqua Jet acts before Kingambit's Sucker Punch, and the two attacks together guarantee the KO if Delphox does not Protect; either attack can also potentially OHKO. This avoids risking Basculegion on a slower Wave Crash while Kingambit can use Sucker Punch and preserves Sneasler to finish Kingambit.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Sneasler as the opposing-Kingambit answer when feasible; Close Combat guarantees the KO on opposing Kingambit and Incineroar at observed levels. Basculegion Aqua Jet resolves before opposing Kingambit's Sucker Punch. Against Mega Delphox, Aqua Jet plus Mega Froslass Shadow Ball guarantees a KO if both connect; either attack individually has only a possible OHKO. Basculegion Wave Crash guarantees an OHKO on Mega Delphox but is vulnerable to Sucker Punch before moving. Mega Delphox's Speed relative to 170-Speed Mega Froslass is uncertain.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Basculegion is dead, so Kingambit's Kowtow is freed to target Froslass. Heat Wave is the key move: it KOs 16% Sneasler through Unburden speed (neutral 95BP spread from 211 SpA) AND chunks Froslass for 62-116%, so King's sure-hit Kowtow then finishes Froslass (~96% combined KO this turn). If Sneasler CCs King (OHKO), King was already expendable — Delphox still KOs Sneasler with Heat Wave and outspeeds the chunked Froslass (204 > 154-189) to finish it next turn. If Sneasler Fake Outs Delphox, Kowtow still lands and next turn Heat Wave double-KOs both low foes before Froslass can move. Sucker Punch is dead vs faster targets, Psyshock wastes the Froslass chip, and Protecting Delphox (streak 2, ~1/3) loses to the CC-King line since doubled CC+SB KOs Delphox even from full.
decisions.notebook: Series 1-0 (G2 late, winning position). Sim rules: Sucker Punch FAILS vs any faster target (dead move — only vs slower 0-priority attackers); consecutive Protect ~1/3; Kowtow Cleave never misses. Sneasler Fake Out deals 12.1–23.3% to Mega Delphox, so Fake Out plus Shadow Ball is not a guaranteed KO. Opposing Life Orb Kingambit Sucker Punch deals 75.5–111% to Mega Froslass. Preserve Sneasler as the opposing-Kingambit answer when feasible; Close Combat guarantees the KO on opposing Kingambit and Incineroar at observed levels. Against Mega Delphox, prioritize controlling Kingambit's Sucker Punch before attacking with Mega Froslass.

decisions.rationale: No legal line can win: Froslass is the only remaining Pokémon, Protect loses to burn damage, and any attack is stopped by Kingambit's priority Sucker Punch from 4% HP. Concede the game and series.

reflections.summary: Won the game and closed the series 2-0. The game was effectively decided at team preview: my Kingambit + Mega Delphox core blanked everything they brought — King resists Froslass-Mega's entire kit and removes Basculegion with Kowtow, while Mega Delphox (204 Spe) outruns both Sneasler's base form and Froslass (189), 4x-Psyshocks Sneasler, and Heat Wave covers both. Their only real breaker, Defiant Kingambit, traded out turn 3 to Incineroar's Flare Blitz (crit-assisted), after which they had no path through the core; their remaining offense (Aqua Jet, resisted CCs, resisted Shadow Balls) only chipped. Variance favored me — the Flare Blitz crit, the Kowtow crit on Basc, the turn-8 Heat Wave burn on Froslass, and one successful consecutive Protect on Delphox — but the position was dominant regardless: even without the burn, Delphox outspeeds and KOs the 9% Froslass. My between-game role plan (King answers Basc/Froslass, Delphox answers Sneasler) worked exactly as designed, so the adjustment helped. Self-inflicted costs that didn't matter: I led Incineroar into their King and fed Defiant +2 again, my Sneasler lost the Adamant mirror (Focus Sash never triggered, taken out by SP chip + resisted CC), and I wasted three Sucker Punches into faster targets under this sim's SP rule before switching to Kowtow Cleave, which immediately produced the Basc KO.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the same four and Mega Delphox — the plan won at preview twice; the fixes are piloting, not construction. (1) Treat Sucker Punch as unclickable against anything faster (in this sim it fails outright); make Kowtow Cleave the default Dark STAB and reserve SP for slower 0-priority attackers only. (2) Stop letting Incineroar's Intimidate proc their Defiant King — switch it in only when their King isn't on the field, or only when Flare Blitz is immediately live to cash the trade. (3) Don't lead my Sneasler into theirs; their Adamant set wins the mirror after any chip and my sash is dead weight — lead Delphox into Sneasler (4x Psyshock, CC only ~46% back) and hold my Sneasler for late Fake Out/Quick Guard utility. (4) Keep the removal order: their King first, then Basc, then Froslass, with Delphox double-Protect stalls to let Kowtow work. Sinistcha-over-Sneasler (CC/Fake Out immune, Rage Powder shields King) remains the standing safety option, but a 2-0 says it isn't needed.
reflections.notebook: Sim rules: Sucker Punch FAILS vs faster targets — only usable vs slower 0-priority attackers; consecutive Protect ~1/3; Kowtow Cleave never misses. Speed ladder: Unburden Sneasler 280-344 > Mega Delphox 204 > Froslass max 189 > my King 71 — Delphox always moves before Froslass. Calcs: Psyshock 4x KOs Sneasler; Sneasler CC only ~46% vs Mega Delphox, but Sneasler CC + Froslass Shadow Ball on the same turn KOs Delphox even from full — never leave Delphox exposed to that double-up without Protect; Heat Wave->Froslass 62-116% and Kowtow->Froslass ~64% from full, so any HW chip makes Kowtow guaranteed; Froslass SB never OHKOs Mega Delphox from full; my King resists Froslass's entire kit and wins that 1v1 easily; snow Blizzard is only ~20% NVE chip. Opponent tendencies: double-targets the immediate/low-HP threat (e.g., Aqua Jet + coverage on the same slot); respects fresh Protects but fires into ones already burned; leans on priority + Protect to blunt Sucker Punch; their Adamant Sneasler wins the mirror vs my Jolly sash set once any chip lands; Mega Froslass sets snow and carries Thunderbolt for Water answers. Strategy: their Defiant King is the only breaker that threatens my core — never Intimidate it (free +2), remove it first via Flare Blitz/Kowtow; after that, King walls Froslass and beats Basculegion while Delphox owns Sneasler — protect those two roles and the matchup closes itself.

reflections.summary: The game was lost primarily because opposing Kingambit survived to control both Mega Froslass and Basculegion, while Mega Delphox used consecutive Protects to stall priority and then cleaned with Heat Wave. Critical hits that removed your boosted Kingambit and Basculegion materially worsened the position, and no piloting errors were recorded. The four brought were workable—Sneasler answered Kingambit, and Mega Froslass pressured Delphox—but they were overly dependent on preserving Sneasler and controlling Sucker Punch. Mega Froslass was a reasonable evolution choice, though it could not reliably KO Delphox and remained highly vulnerable to Kingambit. No game-1 evidence identifies a specific between-game change; whatever adjustment produced this game-2 plan failed to reverse the matchup, resulting in the 0-2 series loss.
reflections.adjustment: In a rematch, preserve Sneasler for opposing Kingambit rather than letting it become heavily weakened in the opening exchange. Prioritize removing or disabling Kingambit before exposing Mega Froslass or Basculegion, and avoid committing attacks into Delphox when Protect plus Kingambit pressure can punish them. The preview plan should reduce the team's shared Kingambit vulnerability; Mega Froslass remains viable only with a clearer Sucker Punch-control plan.

Preserve Sneasler as the opposing-Kingambit answer when feasible; Close Combat guarantees the KO on opposing Kingambit and Incineroar at observed levels. Control Kingambit's Sucker Punch before attacking with Mega Froslass. Opponent is willing to use repeated Sucker Punch attempts and consecutive Mega Delphox Protects to stall priority while Kingambit attacks.

decisions.rationale: Kingambit at 24% is a guaranteed KO for Incineroar's Flare Blitz (52.2-89.1% of full HP), and Incineroar survives even a Helping Hand-boosted +1 LO Kowtow Cleave (max 58.2%), so the Incineroar slot is safe against everything. decisions.rationale: Farigiraf Helping Hand (priority +5) first boosts Raichu-Mega-Y No Guard Focus Blast vs Incineroar. With Mega SpA 160 and HH, 52-95% range becomes ~75%+ vs 66% HP guaranteeing KO through Sitrus and preventing Incineroar Throat Chop (59-85% vs Farigiraf 60%) this turn since Raichu 168 outspeeds Incineroar 80-112. Delphox 169-204 moves before Raichu but Psyshock 56-78% vs Raichu 100% leaves Raichu 22-44% alive, Heat Wave spread even less. KO Incineroar leaves 2v1 vs Delphox 48% with Farigiraf preserved at 60%+Sitrus, better than KO Delphox which still lets Incineroar hit Farigiraf. Mega makes Focus Blast 100% accurate.

Double-target Raichu: Psyshock + Flare Blitz guarantees the KO (min combined 104.8% of its max HP) since it can't Mega Evolve this game and its Fake Out is dead after manually switching in on turn 6. Removing Raichu leaves Farigiraf unable to threaten either of my Pokémon (Psychic immune vs Incineroar, 0.5x vs Delphox), locking the game. Even if Raichu Protects, neither foe can reliably KO my side, and any Trick Room just lets Incineroar move before Raichu next turn.

reflections.summary: Won 1-0 in 9 turns because preview and piloting aligned. Preview: Farigiraf (Armor Tail Sitrus TR/Psychic/Helping Hand/Protect) + Staraptor-Mega + Raichu + Kingambit correctly covered opp's actual 4 (Delphox-Mega/Sneasler/Incineroar/Kingambit) while leaving Blastoise-Mega/Sinistcha (TR/Rage Powder) unbrought. Mega Staraptor (Contrary) over Mega Raichu-Y (No Guard) was correct for this matchup - Contrary Close Combat OHKO'd LO Kingambit T2 and Dual Wingbeat chipped Delphox 39%, despite leaving Raichu as LightningRod (50% Zap Cannon/70% Focus Blast). Piloting: T2-3 double Protect reads blocked Heat Wave + Psyshock + Poison Jab, Farigiraf Psychic broke Sneasler Sash then KO'd, late T8 Trick Room (4 turns left at end) reversed speed vs Timid Delphox, T7 Helping Hand Focus Blast KO'd Incineroar and T9 Psychic + Zap Cannon KO'd Delphox despite accuracy gamble, overcoming crit Psyshock loss of Staraptor T4 and Kingambit trading poorly into Incineroar Flare Blitz x2.
reflections.adjustment: Next game expect opp to bring Blastoise-Mega (Water Spout/Shell Smash) + Sinistcha (TR/Rage Powder/Occa) to counter our TR and redirect. Don't leave LO Kingambit vs Incineroar Flare Blitz - Protect/pivot instead. Time Trick Room earlier or deny theirs, and consider flipping Mega to Raichu-Y for No Guard guaranteed Zap Cannon/Focus Blast vs Delphox/Incineroar rather than relying on 50%/70% LightningRod rolls that hit this game.

reflections.summary: Preview was mostly right — Delphox-Mega was the correct Mega (Psyshock 2x SE removed Mega Staraptor; 204 Spe outspeeds base Raichu) and Sneasler/Incineroar fit, but Kingambit was a dead slot into this four (4x weak to Staraptor's Close Combat, Sucker Punch blanked by Armor Tail) and was OHKO'd without moving. At full HP Delphox survives that exact sequence and KOs Raichu back, so the early chip and losing the anchor — not the final accuracy flip — decided it.

reflections.summary: Lost to +2 Delphox-Mega sweep enabled by preview/piloting gap. Preview: brought Farigiraf/Raichu-Mega-Y/Sylveon/Staraptor (Staraptite) vs Sneasler/Sinistcha/Delphox-Mega/Incineroar (Kingambit/Blastoise benched) and mega-evolved Raichu-Y. Raichu-Y is Psyshock-weak and NoGuard Zap Cannon only para'd Sinistcha, while Staraptor stayed non-mega Intimidate and did 0 relevant damage before OHKO to Psyshock. Piloting: T2 we Protected Farigiraf + Zap Cannon Sinistcha, giving Delphox a free Nasty Plot +2. T3-T4 Sinistcha Rage Powder redirected both Psychics off Delphox onto Sinistcha (39%->8% + Protect stall), so Delphox kept +2 and KO'd Raichu T4, Sylveon T6, Staraptor T8 with Psyshock. Trick Room set T8 at 1-3 down was too late and Farigiraf had no partner damage left.
reflections.adjustment: Next game deny the setup, don't play into Rage Powder. T1-T2 Fake Out or double Psychic/Helping Hand Psychic into Delphox to stop Nasty Plot - ignore 1% Sneasler/Sinistcha. Set Trick Room immediately T1/T2 with Farigiraf while partner pressures Delphox, not T8. Re-evaluate mega: Staraptite (Contrary Close Combat/Dual Wingbeat) pressures Incineroar/Delphox and survives Psyshock better than Raichu-Mega-Y; if bringing Raichu keep it non-mega for Fake Out support or commit to spread damage (Hyper Voice/Heat Wave) to bypass Rage Powder.

reflections.summary: Won by exploiting the opponent's turn-1 Mega Raichu-Y, which locked Staraptor out of Mega all game, while Sinistcha's Rage Powder bought Delphox a free Nasty Plot on turn 2. From there +2 Psyshock ran through Raichu, Sylveon and regular Staraptor, and the opponent's offense couldn't touch my core: Delphox resists their Fairy/Psychic attacks and Incineroar is immune to Farigiraf's only move. Farigiraf's late Trick Room was pure stall and its chained Protects eventually failed. The team-preview plan was right for this matchup: Mega Delphox was the correct holder, Sinistcha redirected and sponged Zap Cannon, Incineroar hard-walled Farigiraf, and Sneasler's Sash absorbed the turn-1 Psychic. Piloting was clean (0 errors, 0 defaults).

reflections.summary: Lost Game 3 and series 1-2 in 7 turns with 0 piloting errors - loss was preview/strategy, not execution. Preview plan backfired: Farigiraf/Sylveon/Kingambit/Staraptor (staraptite) into Delphox-Mega/Sinistcha/Incineroar had no Heat Wave resist and relied on Helping Hand + Pixilate Hyper Voice to bypass Rage Powder. T1 Helping Hand + Hyper Voice into Sinistcha Protect gifted Delphox a free Nasty Plot (+2 to 69% HP) then +2 Psyshock OHKO'd Sylveon, and boosted Heat Wave spread controlled the game. Trick Room war also backfired: cancelling their T2 Trick Room with our own Trick Room removed our speed control, then re-setting TR T4 kept the game under TR where boosted Heat Wave could spread KO Staraptor (T5) and OHKO Kingambit (T6) despite Rage Powder/Protect. Mega choice was wrong: we never Mega Evolved Staraptor (no Contrary value) while opponent correctly Mega Evolved Delphox T1 and swept with it.
reflections.adjustment: In a future series vs this Delphox-Mega/Sinistcha core do not bring Sylveon/Staraptor or Helping Hand into Protect to enable Nasty Plot. Bring a Fire resist/Heat Wave switch-in and single-target pressure that punishes Protect/Nasty Plot turns, and either deny Trick Room with pressure/Taunt or commit to it - do not cancel their TR with your own. If bringing Staraptite must Mega Evolve immediately for Contrary Close Combat value, otherwise bring a different Mega/answer that resists Fire/Psychic and can ignore Rage Powder without relying on spread.

reflections.summary: Won game 3 and the series 2-1 because the between-game adjustment worked exactly as designed: Mega Delphox took +2 SpA via Nasty Plot on turn 1 behind Sinistcha's Protect, comfortably tanking the Helping Hand Hyper Voice (resisted, 70%), then OHKO'd Sylveon with Psyshock while Sinistcha's Trick Room cancelled Farigiraf's, stripping their speed control. From there the Rage Powder + spread-Heat-Wave pattern was airtight: Kingambit's Sucker Punch failed into the redirector, +2 Heat Wave removed Staraptor from full and guaranteed-OHKO'd Kingambit, and Incineroar — the Psychic-immune endgame answer — finished Farigiraf with a super-effective Throat Chop once its Protect chain failed. Piloting was clean (0 decision errors, 7 turns). Team-preview assessment: the four brought (Delphox/Sinistcha/Incineroar/Sneasler) and the Delphoxite Mega choice suited this opponent perfectly — Delphox resists their Fairy/Psychic core, Sinistcha is the hard answer to Farigiraf's TR, Incineroar blanks Farigiraf, and Sneasler covered the Arcanine-H/Kingambit line they ultimately didn't exploit. The opponent adapted between games (new Sylveon TR-mode lead) but not within the game, repeating failed Sucker Punches and Protect-spam into predicted Heat Wave turns.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the same core plan — it is now series-proven — but expect the next adaptation: they already swapped from Raichu+Farigiraf (G1/G2) to Farigiraf+Sylveon TR mode (G3), so a future series may open with Kingambit or Arcanine-H to pressure Delphox before it sets up. Against that, keep Sneasler ready (Close Combat answers both, 4x SE into Kingambit), never let Kingambit target Delphox without Rage Powder active (LO Sucker Punch KOs from ~70%), and never switch Incineroar in while Kingambit lives (Defiant). Preserve Sinistcha better — it was sacked to Kowtow Cleave at 68%; consider Protecting it on predicted Kowtow turns so the TR reversal survives deeper into the game. Continue punishing their Protect-spam habit by doubling into the Protect-reduced slot, exactly as the turn-7 Throat Chop on Farigiraf closed it.
reflections.notebook: OPPONENT TENDENCIES: Adapts between games (G1/G2 led Raichu+Farigiraf w/ Staraptor back; G3 led Farigiraf+Sylveon HH+Hyper Voice TR mode w/ Kingambit+Staraptor back, cutting Raichu and Arcanine-H) but adapts slowly within a game — repeated failed Sucker Punch into Rage Powder, Protect-spams on predicted Heat Wave turns, re-sets TR with a low-HP Farigiraf. Punish by doubling into Protect-reduced slots and KOing the TR resetter the same turn behind Rage Powder. WINNING PATTERN (confirmed G3, 0 errors): Mega Delphox T1 Nasty Plot behind Sinistcha Protect (tanks HH Hyper Voice; resists Fairy/Psychic 0.5x), then attack every turn behind Rage Powder (no consecutive-use fail); Psyshock cleans Sylveon/Raichu/Staraptor, Heat Wave handles Kingambit/Staraptor/Farigiraf; Sinistcha's TR cancels Farigiraf's TR (double-TR cancels regardless of speed order); Incineroar is the safe endgame vs Farigiraf (Psychic-immune, Throat Chop 2x SE) but never switch it into Kingambit (Defiant); Sneasler CC answers Arcanine-H and is 4x SE into Kingambit. KEY MECHANICS: Rage Powder does NOT redirect spread moves (Hyper Voice/Heat Wave bypass) but blanks single-target priority — Kingambit Sucker Punch fails into a Rage Powder user (CONFIRMED); Armor Tail blocks all targeted priority vs its side (Fake Out/Sucker Punch/ESpeed); Hospitality heals Delphox on re-entry; Nasty Plot boosts persist through switches. VERIFIED CALCS: +2 Psyshock OHKOs Sylveon and M-Raichu-Y, 81-156% Staraptor (2x SE if it Megas; even Mega Staraptor is slower than Mega Delphox), only 34-64% vs Calm Farigiraf (never OHKO); +2 Heat Wave guaranteed OHKOs Kingambit, KO'd Staraptor from full (79-156%), 55.9-103.6% Farigiraf, 46-78% Sylveon; Farigiraf Psychic vs Delphox 15-22%, vs Sinistcha 28.7-42.7% neutral, cannot touch Incineroar; LO Sucker Punch guaranteed KOs Delphox from ~70% — keep Rage Powder up; LO Kowtow Cleave KOs Sinistcha below ~85%; Arcanine-H Head Smash 2x SE vs Delphox and 0.25x resists Heat Wave — answer with Sneasler CC; M-Raichu-Y (No Guard Zap Cannon auto-para) sits just under Mega Delphox's speed — Sinistcha resists Electric, eats para, still redirects.
